Looking at the confirm dialog screenshot, I'm checking the frosted glass sheet design with the delete confirmation text, warning color for the image count notice, and the cancel/confirm button styling for contrast and legibility.

I'm also checking sidebar alignment - comparing the "服务状态暂不可用" status text position against the tool icons' x-coordinates to see if the earlier padding fix successfully brought them into near-alignment, which it appears to have done.

The dialog looks near-white with a subtle tint since it's a frosted glass sheet at 0.86 opacity over the blurred backdrop, while the scrim behind dims the whole page and only the dialog itself gets blurred, matching the intended design. I also confirm the "删除" button uses the destructive light-red variant, "取消" is an outline glass pill, and the history toolbar shows a search input, date picker, and segmented control where the active "全部" tab renders as a solid emerald pill with white text.

I removed the dead `dark:aria-invalid` classes from button.tsx, input.tsx, and textarea.tsx since they predate my variant fix, restoring the baseline look without extra cost. Next I need to build the after3 variant, copy it over, and run the benchmark comparing baseline against after3 across the perf scenarios with three repeats each, folding in the confirm/toast scenarios (which just capture screenshots at rep 0 since they have no perf cost) into the same run.

I'm weighing whether including the confirm/toast scenarios adds too much time (~60s extra for load+screenshot per rep), but decide it's worth running everything together since this is the verification of the final state and the total runtime should stay around 7-8 minutes, which is acceptable given the need to confirm the style cost fix didn't regress anything.

Now I'm auditing whether removing dark:aria-invalid actually fixes the style cost issue by checking remaining dark: classes across the codebase—badge, button destructive variant, dropdown-menu destructive item, select, switch, tabs—confirming most only apply to conditionally rendered elements like open menus or specific variants, so they shouldn't add baseline style cost.

Since the base button class had dark:aria-invalid selectors and result cards each have ~6 buttons, removing that eliminates a lot of style computation across hundreds of virtualized buttons. But I'm now questioning whether that's really the culprit versus other changes, like the new "Maximize" chip span added to history cards, which adds extra elements and transforms per card.

I'm also weighing the gradient-background variable resolution on `.studio-result-card`, the transition classes referencing the same easing variables as baseline, and the universal scrollbar rule — trying to figure out which of these is most likely responsible for the roughly 30% increase in style recalculation time during scroll, given baseline style time was around 550ms over a 6-second window.

Since inline transform changes on rows likely only trigger recalculation on the changed element itself (non-inherited properties skip descendants), the real cost seems to come from newly mounted subtrees as day groups enter — each with around 40 elements matched against class, attribute, and universal selector buckets, including my added universal scrollbar rule which every element cheaply matches.

I'm also tracing how the `dark:aria-invalid:border-destructive/50` utility compiles into a nested selector combining the dark theme attribute selector with the aria-invalid attribute selector, and thinking through how right-to-left selector matching handles that compound rule.

I'm uncertain about the exact matching order Blink uses within a compound selector. Separately, I'm considering the media-query variant tied to prefers-color-scheme: dark, which would be inactive under the emulated light scenario, so that block wouldn't apply there.

Removing those dark-mode classes from buttons/inputs/textareas should eliminate matching for the most common elements, but if the style cost doesn't drop it likely points to something else like the universal `*` scrollbar rule. Since each test iteration takes over 7 minutes, I want a more efficient approach — maybe combine the dark-class removal with rescoping scrollbar-color from `*` to just `html`, relying on the fact that scrollbar-color inherits naturally.

But scrollbar-width doesn't inherit, so it needs to stay applied per scroll container, meaning `*` is still the pragmatic choice there unless I target known scroller elements directly. I'm comparing baselines: the desktop shell only applied universal scrollbar rules in the ≥960 media query for desktop runtime, while the wide-mode web baseline lacked such a rule entirely, and I'm noting how the desktop-wide-gen-light baseline's style time compared against that.

Since the descendant-selector scrollbar rule already existed in the desktop baseline without slowing it relative to the web baseline, that rule likely isn't the main cost, and the ~30% style-time increase common to both after-variants points more toward the dark-mode attribute selector switch from a class-based bloom-filter-friendly match to an attribute-based ancestor check that Blink can't reject as cheaply.

I'm also wondering if remaining badges on cards contribute to this, though I'm not certain. After removing these dark: classes, I want to remeasure and see if style time drops back toward baseline, and I'm trying to reconcile the ~175ms style time delta across roughly 6000 frames in wide mode.

Actually, doing the math, style time only accounts for about 3% of the total 6-second run, while the average frame time delta is around 23% — so style recalculation clearly isn't the main driver of the slowdown. That points to something else, likely GPU or compositor related, being the bigger factor.

Looking at the main thread numbers directly: TaskDuration is roughly 5.5 out of 6 seconds, meaning the main thread is about 92% busy, so frame rate is essentially main-thread bound here. Per-frame main thread cost goes from about 0.83ms at baseline up to roughly 1.05ms after the change, which lines up with the frame time regression I'm seeing.

Also the newly mounted day groups add paint cost for their gradients, shadows, and ring/chip elements. I'm second-guessing whether opacity-0 elements actually get skipped during paint in Blink, since I recall some optimization around opacity-0 subtrees but I'm not fully certain of the exact rule.

Confirming that Blink does skip painting invisible-output layers unless there's an active animation or will-change, so the hover overlay stays unpainted at rest. The main added paint cost comes from the gradient backgrounds and box-shadows (inset highlight plus blur) on the new cards, though recording those display items on the main thread is cheap since raster happens separately on GPU.

What's more interesting is the transform on the Maximize chip inside the opacity:0 overlay -- each of these creates its own transform paint property node, which isn't composited but does add paint chunks that PaintArtifactCompositor has to process every frame. Across 100 cards, these extra chunks could add up during the compositor's overlap testing and merge decisions, even if each individual node is cheap.

But since the overlay itself is opacity:0, Blink likely skips painting that invisible subtree entirely, meaning no chunk gets created for the chip in the first place. So that theory falls apart, and I'm circling back to look at whether the card's own transform transition is where the real cost is hiding.

Now I'm looking at how the wide-history card's background changed from a color-mix value to a CSS gradient variable — since gradients are painted as generated images, each card now has to paint and cache its own gradient, which could be a meaningful per-card cost multiplied across many cards.

I'm checking whether the box-shadow and blur-mask filter costs are a factor too, but they seem cheap on GPU raster. So I'm trying to figure out where the extra 0.2ms/frame is actually coming from — since the main thread is nearly saturated in both cases, the bottleneck seems to be there rather than on the GPU side, unless the main thread is somehow blocked waiting on it.

Now I'm tracing what happens per scroll frame: the scrollTop update triggers react-virtual's onScroll, which updates state and forces React to recompute virtual items and re-render the row list. If the card rendering function isn't memoized, every card is re-rendering on every single frame, which would explain a real chunk of that per-frame script cost.

Since row positions (start offsets) only change when measurements update, not every frame, the rows themselves shouldn't be shifting transforms constantly — the actual scrolling is handled by the composited scroller. So most frames should just involve React render work with minimal DOM changes, and style/layout/paint should stay mostly idle unless something else is forcing extra work.

I'm considering ongoing CSS animations that repaint every frame regardless of state—things like the waiting-jobs sweep effect, skeleton pulse placeholders for lazy-loaded images, or the spinning loader icon in the active jobs panel, all of which could explain a small continuous per-frame cost. My new entrance animations finish quickly with a backwards fill so shouldn't be the cause, so I'm now looking at whether the panel's background styling changes are contributing instead.

I check whether the fixed backdrop and background-image elements are static across baseline and after, and conclude they aren't the source. The measurement noise between runs is roughly 2x, making it hard to pin down anything beyond a rough after/baseline ratio of about 1.1-1.2x for wide viewports and 1.07x for normal ones.

Given the "不能影响整体使用性能" constraint, a 0.1-0.2ms per-frame cost is imperceptible in the 60fps budget, so I'm within acceptable territory, though trimming the style cost is still a cheap, worthwhile improvement. I plan to run one more test to confirm, then finalize and report honestly, while also considering removing the resting box-shadow on studio-result-card in wide mode to shave more cost.

Actually, since the drop shadow only affects raster cost at rest rather than per-frame cost, I'll leave it as is. I'm now wondering if the per-frame cost increase actually comes from hover-state invalidation during scroll, since the stationary mouse causes different cards to enter/exit hover as content scrolls beneath it, triggering style recalculation on both baseline and updated versions that share hover rules.

But checking the benchmark setup, the mouse is only moved to (2,2) for screenshot capture, not for the later performance reps, so hover state likely isn't changing during those measurements — and (2,2) sits over the sidebar logo anyway, not the scroller, so this isn't the culprit.

I'm now considering that wrapping Maximize in a new span chip element adds one extra DOM node per card, which means more style and layout work for newly mounted cards during scroll.

The chip's scale/shadow/ring utilities each rely on registered custom properties, and Tailwind v4 registers these via @property, meaning every element using them gets its own non-inherited variable storage that needs computing on layout — this per-element registered-property overhead across many cards could be adding up.

Actually, running the numbers, this only adds negligible cost (roughly 1ms across 100 cards), and the ~30% style time increase translates to just 0.033ms per frame, which isn't nearly enough to explain the overall frame time regression. So style recalculation isn't the real bottleneck here, meaning removing the dark:aria-invalid variant probably wouldn't meaningfully help — I need to look elsewhere for what's actually adding the extra per-frame time.

I'm now considering other candidates during scroll: virtualizer re-renders that skip DOM mutation since values are unchanged, day-change callbacks that only fire occasionally, and the scrollbar thumb rendering itself, especially with thin scrollbar styling possibly interacting oddly with native theme rendering on Windows Chrome.

Actually, custom-colored scrollbars might lose eligibility for the composited-thumb optimization, forcing a main-thread repaint every scroll frame instead of just a compositor move. That per-frame repaint, commit, and raster cycle could plausibly account for the ~0.15ms overhead, matching the baseline (default scrollbar) versus after (custom colors) difference.

I'm fairly confident scrollbar-color was designed by Chrome specifically to avoid forcing main-thread repaints—the thumb only needs repainting on size changes, and scroll offset updates get committed to the compositor the same way regardless of whether scrolling originates from user input or a scrollTop assignment in rAF.

I honestly can't resolve this through pure reasoning; I'd need to isolate variables experimentally, like removing the dark:aria-invalid rule and separately testing whether the global scrollbar-color rule versus the fixed virtual-scroll-container rule is responsible for the behavior difference from baseline.

Given time constraints, running all target/scenario combinations would take too long, so I'll narrow it down to the key regression scenarios (wide-gen-light, wide-gen-dark, and gen-light for history) across the three targets with three repetitions each to get a reasonably confident answer faster.

I'm also reconsidering the scrollbar fix itself: rather than removing the themed thin scrollbars entirely, I could keep the width but rely on `color-scheme: dark` on the root, which makes Chrome render native dark scrollbars automatically without needing custom color rules that might be costing frame time.

With color-scheme dark active, Chrome likely switches to dark native scrollbars, whereas baseline in dark mode had no color-scheme set and thus light ones — that's worth verifying.

My plan: build after3 with the aria-invalid fix, then create after4 by stripping the scrollbar-color declarations from both the global rule and the virtual-scroll-container class, build that too, then benchmark baseline, after3, and after4 across three scenarios with three reps each. Whichever variant matches baseline performance determines which changes to keep.

If both after3 and after4 come out roughly equal to baseline, the scrollbar-color styling is essentially free, so I'd restore it since it looks nicer than plain native scrollbars — meaning I'd need to edit and rebuild once more to land on the final source state. If instead after3 and after4 are both slower than baseline, the performance cost lies elsewhere and I should just accept and report that. I also need to remember to capture the toast screenshot for whichever variant is chosen as final, likely as a separate non-perf run rather than folding it into the benchmark pass.

I'm checking the light-mode results too — normal mode shows history at 0.81ms after vs 0.76ms baseline, basically parity, and window scroll at 0.42ms with no baseline comparison since it wasn't previously scrollable, so the timing budget for two builds plus benchmarking and screenshots fits comfortably. Then I go through the remaining dark-mode class usages to confirm they're low-impact: the badge and dropdown menu destructive-variant classes were already present but dormant in baseline and are now just lightly used, and a handful of other components (settings modal, backup progress, agent generation result, canvas node, toast icon) only have one or two elements affected each, so none of these should meaningfully change the numbers. I'm also noting the removal of certain dark-mode text classes from the tabs trigger component as another minor change to track.

I still need to check remaining dark-mode tab classes for active-state borders and backgrounds — these apply to every tab trigger across sidebar nav and settings, but it's a small enough set to not worry about. Now I'm planning the build sequence: build and copy to after3 for the button/input/textarea edits, then edit globals.css to remove the scrollbar-color rule in two spots (the base layer and the virtual-scroll-container), then build and copy to after4 while kicking off the benchmark in the background. I'll start the first build now, followed by the two CSS edits.

Editing the compiled CSS directly in the after3 output to skip a rebuild is tempting but hacky compared to rebuilding from source, so I'll keep the straightforward sequential build approach for after4.

From the confirm screenshot, things look good — the dialog renders correctly and the sidebar status is now aligned.

具体是用固定的预模糊背景层加光晕颗粒营造氛围，大面板用半透明渐变模拟玻璃感省性能，只在浮层类元素上用真正的backdrop-filter；分了三档玻璃层级，还调整了配色为更深的翡翠绿主色配白字。

顺手还修了几个bug：dark变体一直没生效、字体误用无衬线代替Geist、虚拟滚动容器的滚动条颜色值无效，以及普通网页模式主框架没居中的问题。性能上的关键调整是去掉大面板和列表项上逐个的实时模糊计算，只在页面可滚动时才单独合成背景层，全屏编辑器里看不见的模糊效果也直接去掉了。

还加了对系统"减少透明度"和"减少动态效果"偏好的支持，关闭透明特效时全部变成实色。验证方面构建和类型检查都通过，78个单测全绿，lint的17条警告都是改动前遗留、不在我改动的行里。我在本机用真实GPU合成环境跑了自建基准测试，用80条历史任务数据、关闭帧率上限来测滚动性能，现在需要整理出run3之后的最终中位数结果，做一张场景对比基线与最终值的表。诚实地说，宽屏模式在不限帧时每帧多花约0.1ms，占60Hz帧预算的0.6%左右。

# Skill Authoring

## Overview

Skills are procedural memory: reusable, narrow instructions for task types that are likely to recur. Load this skill when you need to create, rewrite, or patch a workspace skill with `SkillManage`.

Do not create skills for simple one-off answers. A good skill teaches when to use it, what exact steps to follow, what pitfalls to avoid, and how to verify the result.

## When To Use

Use `SkillManage` when:

- A complex task succeeded after several tool calls and produced a reusable workflow.
- A tricky error was fixed and the fix is likely to recur.
- The user explicitly asks you to remember a procedure.
- A user correction revealed a better stable workflow.
- An existing skill was used and found to be stale, incomplete, wrong, or missing a pitfall.

Do not use it for:

- Simple questions, one-off edits, or preferences that belong in memory.
- Speculative workflows that have not been exercised.
- Modifying built-in or user-global skills directly. Create or update a workspace skill instead.

## SkillManage Actions

| Action | Required Parameters | Use For | Example |
|---|---|---|---|
| `create` | `name`, `content` | New reusable workspace skill | `SkillManage(action: "create", name: "debug-api", content: "<full SKILL.md>")` |
| `patch` | `name`, `oldString`, `newString` | Targeted fixes to `SKILL.md` or a supporting file | `SkillManage(action: "patch", name: "debug-api", oldString: "old", newString: "new")` |
| `edit` | `name`, `content` | Full rewrite after reading the current skill | `SkillManage(action: "edit", name: "debug-api", content: "<full updated SKILL.md>")` |
| `write_file` | `name`, `filePath`, `fileContent` | Add or replace supporting files | `SkillManage(action: "write_file", name: "debug-api", filePath: "scripts/check.sh", fileContent: "...")` |
| `remove_file` | `name`, `filePath` | Remove a supporting file | `SkillManage(action: "remove_file", name: "debug-api", filePath: "assets/example.json")` |
| `delete` | `name` | Remove obsolete or harmful workspace skills, only when enabled | `SkillManage(action: "delete", name: "old-skill")` |

Prefer `patch` for small changes. Use `edit` only for major overhauls after reading the current skill.

## Required Frontmatter

Every `SKILL.md` created through `SkillManage` must start with YAML frontmatter:

```yaml
---
name: my-skill
description: One-sentence trigger description
version: 0.1.0
---
```

Rules:

- The file must start with `---` with no leading whitespace.
- `name` must match the `name` parameter.
- `description` should describe the trigger class, not the current task.
- The body must be non-empty and actionable.

## SKILL.md Structure

Use this structure unless a skill has a strong reason to differ:

```markdown
# Title

## Overview
What this skill is for and why it exists.

## When To Use
- Concrete trigger conditions.
- Counter-triggers if useful.

## Workflow
1. Exact steps, commands, files, APIs, or checks.
2. Keep steps specific enough to execute later.

## Common Pitfalls
- Known mistakes and fixes.

## Verification
- How to confirm the workflow succeeded.
```

## Supporting Files

Supporting files must stay inside the skill directory under one of:

- `scripts/` for helper scripts.
- `assets/` for static assets.

Use `write_file` for supporting files. Use `patch` with `filePath` for targeted edits to supporting files. Absolute paths and `..` traversal are rejected.

## Size Limits

- `SkillManage` enforces size limits for `SKILL.md` and supporting files.
- If a skill is growing too large, keep `SKILL.md` focused on triggers, workflow, pitfalls, and verification. Put executable helpers in `scripts/` and static examples in `assets/`.

## Common Pitfalls

1. Writing a broad skill that tries to cover an entire domain. Split by trigger and workflow.
2. Omitting exact commands, paths, or verification steps. Future use needs concrete instructions.
3. Expecting a newly created skill to be available immediately in the current pro

# Skill Authoring

## Overview

Skills are procedural memory: reusable, narrow instructions for task types that are likely to recur. Load this skill when you need to create, rewrite, or patch a workspace skill with `SkillManage`.

Do not create skills for simple one-off answers. A good skill teaches when to use it, what exact steps to follow, what pitfalls to avoid, and how to verify the result.

## When To Use

Use `SkillManage` when:

- A complex task succeeded after several tool calls and produced a reusable workflow.
- A tricky error was fixed and the fix is likely to recur.
- The user explicitly asks you to remember a procedure.
- A user correction revealed a better stable workflow.
- An existing skill was used and found to be stale, incomplete, wrong, or missing a pitfall.

Do not use it for:

- Simple questions, one-off edits, or preferences that belong in memory.
- Speculative workflows that have not been exercised.
- Modifying built-in or user-global skills directly. Create or update a workspace skill instead.

## SkillManage Actions

| Action | Required Parameters | Use For | Example |
|---|---|---|---|
| `create` | `name`, `content` | New reusable workspace skill | `SkillManage(action: "create", name: "debug-api", content: "<full SKILL.md>")` |
| `patch` | `name`, `oldString`, `newString` | Targeted fixes to `SKILL.md` or a supporting file | `SkillManage(action: "patch", name: "debug-api", oldString: "old", newString: "new")` |
| `edit` | `name`, `content` | Full rewrite after reading the current skill | `SkillManage(action: "edit", name: "debug-api", content: "<full updated SKILL.md>")` |
| `write_file` | `name`, `filePath`, `fileContent` | Add or replace supporting files | `SkillManage(action: "write_file", name: "debug-api", filePath: "scripts/check.sh", fileContent: "...")` |
| `remove_file` | `name`, `filePath` | Remove a supporting file | `SkillManage(action: "remove_file", name: "debug-api", filePath: "assets/example.json")` |
| `delete` | `name` | Remove obsolete or harmful workspace skills, only when enabled | `SkillManage(action: "delete", name: "old-skill")` |

Prefer `patch` for small changes. Use `edit` only for major overhauls after reading the current skill.

## Required Frontmatter

Every `SKILL.md` created through `SkillManage` must start with YAML frontmatter:

```yaml
---
name: my-skill
description: One-sentence trigger description
version: 0.1.0
---
```

Rules:

- The file must start with `---` with no leading whitespace.
- `name` must match the `name` parameter.
- `description` should describe the trigger class, not the current task.
- The body must be non-empty and actionable.

## SKILL.md Structure

Use this structure unless a skill has a strong reason to differ:

```markdown
# Title

## Overview
What this skill is for and why it exists.

## When To Use
- Concrete trigger conditions.
- Counter-triggers if useful.

## Workflow
1. Exact steps, commands, files, APIs, or checks.
2. Keep steps specific enough to execute later.

## Common Pitfalls
- Known mistakes and fixes.

## Verification
- How to confirm the workflow succeeded.
```

## Supporting Files

Supporting files must stay inside the skill directory under one of:

- `scripts/` for helper scripts.
- `assets/` for static assets.

Use `write_file` for supporting files. Use `patch` with `filePath` for targeted edits to supporting files. Absolute paths and `..` traversal are rejected.

## Size Limits

- `SkillManage` enforces size limits for `SKILL.md` and supporting files.
- If a skill is growing too large, keep `SKILL.md` focused on triggers, workflow, pitfalls, and verification. Put executable helpers in `scripts/` and static examples in `assets/`.

## Common Pitfalls

1. Writing a broad skill that tries to cover an entire domain. Split by trigger and workflow.
2. Omitting exact commands, paths, or verification steps. Future use needs concrete instructions.
3. Expecting a newly created skill to be available immediately in the current prompt. It is picked up on the next turn or session refresh.

## Verification

Before finishing, confirm the frontmatter starts at byte 0 and includes `name`, `description`, and `version`; `name` matches the directory and the `SkillManage` request; the description explains when to use the skill; the body includes workflow, pitfalls, and verification guidance; supporting files stay under `scripts/` or `assets/`; and the skill is narrow enough to be reused without confusion.

--- name: nova-ui-perf-check description: Measure before/after scroll frame times and capture screenshots for nova-image-studio frontend styling changes with a dependency-free CDP harness on the cached headless Chromium. Use when a frontend restyle (globals.css, ui primitives, shell) must be shown not to regress performance. version: 0.1.0 --- # Nova UI Performance Check ## Overview Compare a baseline and a changed static export of `frontend/` side by side. Local static servers, Playwright's cached Chromium driven over raw CDP (no npm installs), seeded history data, screenshots, and scroll frame timings. ## When To Use - Visual or CSS changes to nova-image-studio where the user requires no performance impact. - Not for backend or API performance. ## Workflow 1. Baseline before editing: `cd frontend; $env:NOVA_DESKTOP_BUILD='1'; npm run build` (PWA off, so `public/sw.js` is not regenerated), then copy `frontend/out` to `%TEMP%\nova-ui-bench\baseline`. After changes, copy each build to a new folder (`after`, `after2`, ...); never overwrite a copy. 2. Harness (`%TEMP%\nova-ui-bench\bench.mjs`, Node 24 ESM; recreate if missing): - Static server per build on 127.0.0.1. `/api/*` returns 404 JSON and WebSocket upgrades are destroyed, which matches the app running without its backend. - Chromium: `%LOCALAPPDATA%\ms-playwright\chromium-1228\chrome-win64\chrome.exe --headless=new --remote-debugging-port=

--user-data-dir= --ignore-gpu-blocklist --enable-gpu-rasterization --disable-gpu-vsync --disable-frame-rate-limit`. Headless still uses the real GPU; confirm with `SystemInfo.getInfo`. - CDP over Node's global `WebSocket`: `Target.createTarget`, then `Target.attachToTarget({ flatten: true })`. - Per page, `Page.addScriptToEvaluateOnNewDocument` sets localStorage `theme` and `nova-wide-mode` (`enabled`/`disabled`). For desktop styling it also defines a fake `window.novaDesktop` (config maps to localStorage, `records.list('image-records')` reads IndexedDB, other methods return empty results). - Seed once per origin: localStorage `nova-jobs` (jobs without image fields) plus IndexedDB `nova-image-db` version 2, store `images`, records `{ id, jobId, status, imageData, images, refImages, error }` with canvas-generated base64 PNGs. Use about 80 jobs over 10 days, because the history list is virtualized per day group. - Scroll `.studio-history-list` in requestAnimationFrame along a time-based cosine path (about 6 s) at device scale factor 1.5. Record frame deltas (avg, p95, p99, share above 17.5 ms) and `Performance.getMetrics` deltas (`TaskDuration`, `RecalcStyleDuration`, `LayoutDuration`). Count elements whose computed `backdrop-filter` is not `none`. 3. Run all targets in one browser session, interleaved per repetition (A,B then B,A), with 3 repetitions; compare medians. Run in the background and poll the log; a full run takes 6-8 minutes. 4. When a delta appears, build variants that each change one suspect and measure them together instead of reasoning about the cause. ## Common Pitfalls - Wide mode renders hidden header duplicates of sidebar buttons (`随机图片`, `设置`): always click the first visible match. - The settings dialog only scrolls at the Electron minimum height (1440x680). - The history card delete button title is `移除` (its dialog title is `删除记录`). The single-image `添加到素材库` button fires an image-action toast; multi-image cards use a dropdown trigger (`aria-haspopup`). - Run-to-run noise is about 2x (the same baseline measured 0.9 ms and 2.0 ms average). For performance, large panels avoid real-time blur entirely, relying instead on a fixed background layer drawn once with semi-transparent gradients to fake the glass look — real-time backdrop-filter is reserved for small floating elements only. The count of live-blur elements on screen at idle stays at 0 both before and after these changes, only appearing when menus, dialogs, toasts, or the canvas floating toolbar are open (2 elements on the canvas page).

I'm also removing per-item blur buttons on list entries (agent images, prompt plaza, attachment thumbnails) in favor of semi-transparent dark backgrounds with inner borders, stripping the barely-visible blur from fullscreen editors sitting on 95%-opaque backgrounds (GIF frame adjuster, canvas nodes, annotation editor), and making the settings dialog a near-opaque static panel since it's large and scrolls. I'm wiring this up to follow the system's "transparency effects: off" setting by switching to solid colors, and disabling entrance animations when "reduce motion" is on.

Now I'm looking at benchmark results comparing before/after frame timings across normal mode, wide light mode, and wide dark mode history scrolling — checking average frame cost, p95, and the percentage of frames exceeding 17ms, trying to figure out which run to use for the dark mode comparison since the numbers are close.

I've decided the fairest approach is to report the final build's numbers for dark mode while noting that machine state introduced some noise between runs, rather than cherry-picking the more favorable earlier measurement.

I also traced the wide-screen slowdown to the fixed background layer staying promoted to its own compositing layer permanently; fixing it so promotion only happens during scroll brought performance back in line. The scrollbar-color hypothesis turned out to have no effect, and CSS bundle size grew from 145.5KB to 155.7KB (+7%). Along the way I also caught that the `dark:` variant was never actually activating since it targets a `.dark` class while the project switches themes via `data-theme`.

Fixing that got the dark styles working properly for the model editor and backup progress bars. I also found `font-mono` was silently falling back to sans-serif due to an undefined `--font-geist-mono` variable, the history list scrollbar was using an invalid `hsl(var(--hex))` value, the main frame wasn't centered in regular web mode, and text contrast on the primary color jumped from ~2.6:1 to ~4.9:1, bringing warning and danger colors up to AA as well. Verification-wise, the full build passed with PWA restored, all 78 unit tests passed, and lint showed the same pre-existing 8 errors and 9 warnings untouched by my changes.

I covered screenshots across light/dark, web/desktop, and normal/wide layouts, plus dropdown menus, card hovers, settings modal, confirmation dialogs, toasts, the infinite canvas, and my assets page — the React #418 hydration warning exists both before and after my changes, so it's a pre-existing issue. A few things worth flagging: the performance numbers come from headless Chromium on the same GPU but aren't from an actual Electron window, three pages (prompt reversal, GIF generation, prompt plaza) inherited the new styles via shared tokens and base components but weren't individually screenshotted, the mint-colored focus box on the first settings tab is a pre-existing style, and if Windows has "transparency effects" disabled, users will see the solid fallback version, which is intentional. Desktop needs a rebuild to reflect the changes, which happens automatically with the dev command, and all before/after screenshots and test reports are saved locally with the baseline in its own folder.

I saved this whole testing workflow as a reusable workspace skill so I can run the same comparison quickly next time I touch the UI. I'm also double-checking the idle blur element count — for the canvas page specifically, once a canvas is created the toolbar and zoom controls both use backdrop blur, so I want to verify that count matches between baseline and the final version.

I could also add a fourth row for the settings dialog scroll, showing it's unaffected: roughly 4.53→4.65ms with 5.4ms consistently, essentially 0% change either way.

I want to note honestly that during the wide+dark run the machine seemed slower overall (~2ms both sides), while another comparable run showed 0.92→1.11ms with over-17ms frame share staying flat at 0.4%→0.4%. The wide mode overhead looks like roughly 0.1–0.35ms per frame depending on the run. UI 已改成"极光玻璃"风格，性能和改动前基本持平。品牌色仍是薄荷绿。背景改成一个固定层，由预模糊的自然图、柔和极光和细颗粒组成。侧栏、面板和卡片分层做成半透明玻璃，下拉菜单、弹层、Toast、确认框和画布工具栏用真正的毛玻璃。改动还没有提交。

**改了什么**

- [globals.css](frontend/src/app/globals.css)：新的亮色和暗色设计 token、固定背景层、三档玻璃表面、浮层玻璃样式，以及布局和入场动效。
- 基础组件：
  - 主按钮改成深翡翠绿，带一点光晕；描边按钮改成玻璃胶囊。
  - 输入框、下拉、选择器、弹层、提示、对话框、标签页、开关、滑块和分段控件统一成同一套风格。
- 外框和常用组件：
  - 侧栏当前项是凸起的胶囊，左边有一条小指示条。
  - 常规模式下主框架居中浮起。
  - [Toast.tsx](frontend/src/components/workspace/Toast.tsx) 重写成玻璃胶囊，左侧是图标。
  - 结果卡片悬停时显示渐变遮罩和一个玻璃按钮。
- [utils.ts](frontend/src/lib/utils.ts)：在 `cn()` 里注册了新加的阴影类，这样 `shadow-none` 这类覆盖能正确生效。

**性能上怎么做的**

- 大面板不做实时模糊。固定背景层只绘制一次，面板是叠在上面的半透明渐变。
- 实时模糊只用在小浮层上。页面空闲时，改动前后正在渲染的模糊元素都是 0 个。画布页有 2 个（浮动工具栏和缩放控件），这两个原来就带模糊。
- 列表项上逐个带模糊的悬停按钮（Agent 图片、提示词广场、附件缩略图）改成半透明深色加内描边，不再模糊。
- 几个全屏编辑器的底色本来就是 95% 不透明，上面的模糊几乎看不见，已去掉。
- 设置弹窗面积大、需要滚动，改成接近不透明的静态面板。
- 系统里关闭"透明效果"时自动显示实色版本；开启"减少动态效果"时关闭入场动画。

**对比测试**

测试条件：本机 Chromium 149，Intel UHD 770 显卡，80 条历史任务，不限帧滚动 6 秒，改前和改后交替跑 3 轮，取中位数。

| 场景 | 平均帧耗时（改前 → 改后） | p95 | 超 17ms 的帧占比 |
|---|---|---|---|
| 常规模式，历史滚动 | 0.75 → 0.84ms | 1.8 → 2.0ms | 0.2% → 0.2% |
| 宽屏亮色，历史滚动 | 0.95 → 1.04ms | 3.5 → 3.1ms | 0.4% → 0.3% |
| 宽屏暗色，历史滚动 | 1.99 → 2.35ms | 6.1 → 6.7ms | 1.0% → 1.3% |
| 设置弹窗滚动 | 4.53 → 4.65ms | 5.4 → 5.4ms | 0% → 0% |

宽屏暗色这一行测的时候机器偏慢，两边都在 2ms 左右。另一轮用的是只差一处小修复的版本，结果是 0.92 → 1.11ms，超 17ms 的帧占比 0.4% → 0.4%。总体看，宽屏每帧多出约 0.1 到 0.35ms，不到 60Hz 下每帧时间预算的 2%。

第一版的宽屏帧耗时比改动前高 17% 到 30%。原因是固定背景层一直单独占着一个合成层。改成只在页面本身能滚动时才单独合成后，降到了上表的水平。CSS 体积从 145.5KB 增加到 155.7KB，多了 7%。

**顺手修掉的原有问题**

- `dark:` 暗色样式一直没生效：它依赖 `.dark` 类，而项目是用 `data-theme` 切换主题的。现在它跟随 `data-theme` 和系统设置，设置里的模型编辑区、备份进度条等原本写好的暗色样式开始生效。
- `font-mono` 引用了一个从未定义的变量，实际显示成普通无衬线字体。现在代码块和队列里的数字都用等宽字体。
- 历史列表滚动条的颜色写的是无效值，现在跟随主题色。
- 常规网页模式的主框架没有居中，一直贴在左上角。
- 主色配白字的对比度从约 2.6:1 提到约 4.9:1；警告色和危险色的文字也达到了 WCAG AA 的对比度要求。

**验证**

- 正式构建通过，TypeScript 和 CSS 都没有报错。最后一次构建已恢复 PWA。
- 78 个单测全部通过。
- lint 还是改动前的 8 个错误、9 个警告，都不在我改过的行上。
- 截图覆盖了亮色和暗色、网页和桌面、常规和宽屏，以及下拉、悬停、设置、确认框、Toast、画布和素材页。
- React #418 水合警告在改动前就存在，改动前后次数一样。

**需要注意**

- 测试是在同一块显卡上用无头 Chromium 跑的，不是真实的 Electron 窗口。
- 反推提示词、动图生成、提示词广场这三页通过公共样式继承了新风格，但没有单独截图检查。
- 设置弹窗第一个标签上的薄荷色方框是原本就有的焦点样式，不是这次改出来的。
- 如果 Windows 关了"透明效果"，看到的会是实色版本，这是有意的回退。
- 桌面端需要重新构建才能看到效果，`npm run desktop:dev` 会自动构建。

改前改后的截图和测试报告在 `%TEMP%\nova-ui-bench`，约 30MB，看完可以删掉：`shots\baseline` 是改前，`shots\after` 是第一版，`shots\after3` 是最终版的 Toast、确认框、画布和素材页截图。这套测试流程我记成了工作区技能 `nova-ui-perf-check`，以后改 UI 可以直接复用。

I've gathered enough evidence from the code, so now I should check the actual failed task records in the database to find the real error messages, since the desktop DB should have this information.

I know from the code that for image models with the 'openai' protocol, the backend calls the standard OpenAI Images API endpoints — text-to-image generations or image-to-image edits with multipart uploads — so the protocol itself matches, but it's not necessarily a minimal or fully compliant request; the base URL is user-configured, which could be a source of failure.

The trailing `/v1` in the user's base URL gets stripped and then re-appended before the images path, which works for standard configurations but breaks for providers whose base URL doesn't follow that exact convention — like ones with custom API version paths (e.g. `/api/v3`) or nested paths without `/v1`. That's a real divergence from how the official OpenAI SDK composes URLs, since the SDK expects the base_url to already include `/v1` and just appends the endpoint, whereas this project forcibly re-inserts `/v1` regardless of what's already there.

I'm also noting the streaming fallback logic depends on matching specific error message patterns to detect "stream unsupported" — but many relay providers return generic or differently-worded errors, or accept the stream flag but respond in a non-OpenAI-compatible SSE format, which would cause silent failures rather than a graceful fallback.

Another possibility is a relay that fails silently or returns an error not matching expected patterns, or an unparseable stream. +# Read-only: list failed image jobs and the image-model configs they used.
+# Prints model/protocol/baseUrl/size/error only. Never prints prompts, API keys or app_secrets.
+import json
+import os
+import pathlib
+import sqlite3
+
+ROOT = pathlib.Path(os.environ["LOCALAPPDATA"]) / "Nova Image Studio" / "data"
+WEB_DB = pathlib.Path(r"F:\项目\nova-image-studio\backend\nova-tasks.sqlite")
+SECRET_FIELDS = {"apiKey", "api_key", "key", "token", "secret", "password"}
+
+
+def ro(path):
+    return sqlite3.connect(path.resolve().as_uri() + "?mode=ro", uri=True)
+
+
+def clip(value, n=260):
+    text = str(value or "").replace("\n", " ").strip()
+    return text if len(text) <= n else text[:n] + " …"
+
+
+def dump_task_db(path):
+    if not path.exists():
+        print(f"(no {path})")
+        return
+    con = ro(path)
+    rows = con.execute(
+        "SELECT id, status, error, created_at, request_json FROM tasks "
+        "WHERE status = 'failed' OR (error IS NOT NULL AND error != '') ORDER BY created_at DESC LIMIT 25"
+    ).fetchall()
+    print(f"\n== {path} : {len(rows)} failed tasks ==")
+    for task_id, status, error, created_at, request_json in rows:
+        req = json.loads(request_json or "{}")
+        print(f"- {created_at} {status} protocol={req.get('protocol')} model={req.get('model')} "
+              f"baseUrl={req.get('baseUrl')} mode={req.get('mode')} size={req.get('outputSize')} "
+              f"ratio={req.get('aspectRatio')} custom={req.get('customSize') or '-'} "
+              f"quality={req.get('gptImageQuality')} bg={req.get('gptImageBackground')}")
+        print(f"    task error: {clip(error)}")
+        for idx, item_status, item_error in con.execute(
+            "SELECT item_index, status, error FROM task_items WHERE task_id = ? AND error IS NOT NULL AND error != ''",
+            (task_id,),
+        ):
+            if item_error != error:
+                print(f"    item[{idx}] {item_status}: {clip(item_error)}")
+    con.close()
+
+
+dump_task_db(ROOT / "tasks.sqlite")
+dump_task_db(WEB_DB)
+
+app_db = ROOT / "app.sqlite"
+if app_db.exists():
+    con = ro(app_db)
+    keys = con.execute("SELECT namespace, storage_key, length(value_json) FROM app_settings ORDER BY storage_key").fetchall()
+    print("\n== app_settings keys ==", ", ".join(f"{k}({n})" for _, k, n in keys))
+    for namespace, key, _ in keys:
+        raw = con.execute("SELECT value_json FROM app_settings WHERE namespace = ? AND storage_key = ?", (namespace, key)).fetchone()[0]
+        try:
+            value = json.loads(raw)
+            if isinstance(value, str):
+                value = json.loads(value)
+        except (ValueError, TypeError):
+            continue
+        if key == "nova-jobs" and isinstance(value, list):
+            failed = [j for j in value if isinstance(j, dict) and j.get("status") == "failed"]
+            print(f"\n== history jobs: {len(value)} total, {len(failed)} failed (newest first) ==")
+            for job in sorted(failed, key=lambda j: j.get("created_at", ""), reverse=True)[:25]:

+                      f"server={'yes' if job.get('serverTaskId') else 'no'} error={clip(job.get('error'))}")
+        elif isinstance(value, dict) and isinstance(value.get("imageModels"), list):

The user is asking whether the GPT image generation models in their system use standard OpenAI protocol, and why some endpoints fail in the current project but succeed when used directly with the standard protocol using the same address and key. Checking the task database, I don't see any failed tasks recorded there.

Looking at the configured image models, five are set up, four using OpenAI protocol across different endpoints like aioss.cc and xianapi.cloud with models like gpt-image-2. All show hasApiKey as false in app_settings, but that's just because keys are actually stored separately in encrypted app_secrets, not because keys are missing.

The xianapi.cloud endpoint with gpt-image-2-4k is a likely candidate for failures, though I can't confirm without direct error logs. I now want to compare the actual request format the backend sends to the OpenAI Images API against what a minimal standard request would look like, since the backend likely adds extra fields beyond just model, prompt, and size that a strict OpenAI-compatible relay might reject.

Streaming is enabled by default, so requests always include stream and partial_images flags—but the fallback to non-streaming only triggers on specific error message patterns. If a relay fails differently, like with generic errors, timeouts, or malformed SSE responses that the parser doesn't recognize, there's no fallback path and the task simply fails.

Tracing through the SSE parsing logic, standard OpenAI-format streaming events for image generation should parse correctly since the parser checks for b64_json at multiple nesting levels and skips partial image events appropriately. The bigger issue is that relays might emit non-standard formats that break this parsing. I'm also noting that quality, background, and output_format parameters are always sent with defaults since the advanced params object is always truthy in the request builder.

That test file confirms this forwarding behavior is intentional. Now I'm checking the size calculation logic — for 1K with 16:9 aspect ratio, it rounds to a multiple of 16, giving something like 1824x1024.

I'm noticing there's a size limit config in the code, so the relay's "gpt-image-2" might actually be routing to a different backend that rejects or ignores arbitrary sizes like 3840x2160 for 4K requests, while smaller default sizes like 1024x1024 still work fine.

For 1:1 with 4K, side becomes 3840, and '512' returns undefined for size. Now I'm thinking about how the backend handles the base URL — it strips a trailing `/v1` and always appends `/v1/images/generations`, matching the OpenAI SDK convention where `base_url` ending in `/v1` gets `/images/generations` appended, so `https://host` correctly becomes `https://host/v1/images/generations`.

Testing this against several real provider URLs, I notice many break: paths like `/v1beta/openai`, `/api/v3`, or `/api/paas/v4` end up with a duplicated or wrong version segment, producing a 404 that returns an HTML error page instead of JSON. The user's xianapi.cloud address has no extra path so it's fine, but this logic would fail for other providers they might try. I'm also noting that the response parser only accepts string values from specific fields like `b64_json`, `url`, or `image_url`, either top-level or nested under `result/response/output`.

I'm also not fully certain how the code handles downloading from a returned URL — there's a fetch call around line 488 that likely proxies the download, but if the URL expires quickly or blocks hotlinking, that could be another failure point worth flagging cautiously.

On image-to-image, I'm weighing whether the multipart field naming for multiple reference images (`image` vs `image[]`) could trip up some relays, but I'm not confident enough about OpenAI's actual behavior here to state it firmly, so I'll likely leave this out and stay focused on the things I've actually verified.

I'm also considering parallelCount behavior—whether multiple generation requests run concurrently and could hit relay rate limits causing partial failures—but since I haven't confirmed the concurrency model, I'll skip that too. Similarly, gateway timeouts on long 4K generations are plausible but too generic to call out specifically, so I'm moving toward the text model section where the base URL for text models appears to be hardcoded to a fixed domain.

生图模型的地址是真正生效的，这点在配置代码里保持一致。另外检查本地数据发现，桌面端任务库和历史nova-jobs记录里都没有失败任务留存——可能是TTL清理了，或者失败发生在网页版而非客户端。

图像模型配置了4个openai协议条目，还有一个第三方地址xianapi.cloud用的gpt-image-2，4K规格；密钥都加密单独存放在app_secrets里，我没有读取，得跟用户说明这点，避免误导。基本判断是走OpenAI Images协议而非chat completions，但不是最简标准调用，需要按可能性列出差异点，并建议用户设置环境变量关闭流式来验证。

同时想到几个改进方向：让流式失败时的回退更健壮，不只匹配特定报错还要覆盖任意失败情况，改成失败后自动重试一次非流式；或者干脆加个per-model的"流式返回"开关，第三方地址默认关闭；另外quality/background/output_format这些参数只有在supportsAdvancedParams开启且取值不是默认值时才发送。

关于base URL兼容性,还要考虑用户地址已经带版本号（如/v3、/v4）的情况，这时应该直接拼接/images/generations而不是强行加/v1前缀，同时响应解析要兼容image_url.url对象格式和markdown图片链接两种返回形式。

现在琢磨用户怎么在桌面模式下关闭流式——需要设置环境变量NOVA_IMAGE_STREAM=false传给后端进程,但不确定backend-process.js是否会把这个变量正确传递给子进程；对于web/docker模式，得查一下server.js里loadEnvFile()具体读取的是哪个.env文件，这块我还没有完全确认，得跟用户说清楚这是推测而非确定的信息。

最终我倾向于只说明后端确实支持NOVA_IMAGE_STREAM=false这个环境变量（这个是有代码依据的），但不去猜测桌面版具体怎么设置，而是主动提出可以帮忙加一个界面开关。同时因为本地没有失败记录了，我应该先问用户失败卡片显示的具体报错文本，再决定要不要动手修复——按现在的情况，用户是在问原因，我应该先分析解释,然后再简短地提出可以帮忙修的选项，不用长篇展开。

至于之前那个诊断脚本，留在临时目录里问题不大，用户已经知道那个文件夹可以整个删掉，我就不专门再去清理这一个文件了。

另外，用户提到用标准OpenAI协议、相同地址和密钥就能生成成功，这说明大模型可能只是发了一个最简单的非流式调用，没有加额外参数——这正好支持我之前关于流式处理的猜测方向。

我还确认了advancedParams对象总是会被填充默认值，quality/background/output_format等参数始终会被附加进请求，style只在vivid/natural时生效，前端的supportsAdvancedParams只是控制UI显示，后端并不理会这个标志。同时我在检查错误匹配模式时，发现类似"Unknown parameter: 'stream'"这种400错误正好能被现有的正则模式捕获到。

但我担心的是那些不匹配这个模式的失败场景——比如上游负载饱和、500错误或upstream error这类提示，都不会被识别为"不支持stream"的情况。另外，如果relay接受了stream参数但用不同的事件名格式返回SSE数据（比如Responses API风格的response.output_item.done事件，其中item.result是base64字符串），现有的isPartialImageEvent和getImagePayloadValue逻辑可能无法正确解析这种嵌套结构。

我发现真正的问题是：解析器只认b64_json、url、image_url这几个字段，而且值必须是字符串——像image_url是对象嵌套、Responses格式里result直接放base64字符串、或者正文用Markdown图片链接返回的情况，都会因为解析不到而报"响应中无图片数据"这个模糊的错误。我打算把这一点整合进解析器那条要点里，同时也该说明用户看到不同错误提示时该怎么自我诊断，比如路径错误时会看到"上游返回了HTML页面而不是JSON"这样的提示。

I've gathered enough evidence from the code, so now I should check the actual failed task records in the database to find the real error messages, since the desktop DB should have this information.

I know from the code that for image models with the 'openai' protocol, the backend calls the standard OpenAI Images API endpoints — text-to-image generations or image-to-image edits with multipart uploads — so the protocol itself matches, but it's not necessarily a minimal or fully compliant request; the base URL is user-configured, which could be a source of failure.

The trailing `/v1` in the user's base URL gets stripped and then re-appended before the images path, which works for standard configurations but breaks for providers whose base URL doesn't follow that exact convention — like ones with custom API version paths (e.g. `/api/v3`) or nested paths without `/v1`. That's a real divergence from how the official OpenAI SDK composes URLs, since the SDK expects the base_url to already include `/v1` and just appends the endpoint, whereas this project forcibly re-inserts `/v1` regardless of what's already there.

I'm also noting the streaming fallback logic depends on matching specific error message patterns to detect "stream unsupported" — but many relay providers return generic or differently-worded errors, or accept the stream flag but respond in a non-OpenAI-compatible SSE format, which would cause silent failures rather than a graceful fallback.

Another possibility is a relay that fails silently or returns an error not matching expected patterns, or an unparseable stream. I'm also noting that the request always includes extra params like quality, background, and output format since the advanced params normalizer always supplies defaults, so these extra fields get sent to OpenAI even when unspecified by the user.

But for DALL·E 3 upstreams, background and output_format aren't valid params and would trigger a 400 error, so any relay routing to DALL·E 3 breaks. Same risk for OpenAI-compatible endpoints fronting other models like Flux or Doubao Seedream, where strict validation might reject these fields too.

The gpt-image params test explicitly asserts these get forwarded, so the design intent is confirmed. I'm also checking that `n` is only sent via multipart, not JSON, and that image arrays stay empty for text-to-image mode. Then I'm tracing the size resolution logic — custom sizes up to 4096 in multiples of 16, or computed sizes based on aspect ratio.

But if the actual upstream model is gpt-image-1, those computed sizes for non-1:1 ratios (like 1824x1024) wouldn't be valid — gpt-image-1 only accepts 1024x1024, 1536x1024, 1024x1536, or auto, so this could produce a 400 error. A plain OpenAI call omitting size or using a standard value would work fine, so the discrepancy points to the relay sending non-standard computed sizes for non-square aspect ratios.

I'm also checking how the response payload gets parsed — looking for b64_json, url, or image_url fields either nested under a data array or at the top level.

There's a tricky edge case: if image_url comes back as an object like `{url}` rather than a plain string, the normalizer will fail to recognize it as a string and throw the "no image data" error instead of continuing to check other fields. I'm also noting that when a relay returns a plain URL, the frontend just downloads it directly.

Some relays might return short-lived or CORS-blocked URLs, which could cause the frontend to fail on download even if the response itself contained valid data—matching the user's complaint about the image not returning successfully. I also want to check whether certain image models expose themselves through chat completions with markdown links in the content, rather than the standard image generation endpoint, since that changes where I need to look for the actual image data.

That the user's other agent succeeded using the standard OpenAI protocol with the same address and key suggests the difference lies in how this codebase composes the request—streaming flags, extra parameters, size, or URL construction—rather than the credentials themselves. Timeout settings look fine at 30 minutes, so I can rule those out as the cause.

The likely culprits are the project defaulting to `stream: true` with `partial_images: 1` on the first attempt, with fallback only triggering on a narrow regex match—meaning relays that fail differently or return nonstandard SSE formats will break without recovering. On top of that, it always sends `quality: auto`, `background: auto`, and `output_format: png` regardless of whether the model actually supports these advanced parameters, which could be rejected by stricter relays.

It also computes non-standard `size` values from aspect ratio and resolution (like 16:9 at 1K becoming 1824x1024), which only works for gpt-image-2-class models since gpt-image-1 and others have fixed allowed size lists. Additionally, the URL logic strips any trailing `/v1` and always re-appends `/v1/images/...`, unlike the OpenAI SDK which just appends `/images/...` to the base_url directly—this could break endpoints using a different version segment.

Response parsing also only recognizes specific fields like `data[].b64_json/url/image_url` as strings, so nested `image_url: {url}` objects or chat-completion-style replies won't be detected, producing a "no image data in response" error. For image-to-image, I'm also considering how the multipart `image` field is sent—some relays might expect `image[]` instead of repeated `image` fields, and I'm uncertain whether OpenAI's actual behavior matches standard array-style multipart encoding.

Since the user's report is likely about text-to-image failures, I'll skip that hedge. I'm also noting that the text model's base URL is hard-coded to a fixed value, and the normalization and URL-building logic seem to ignore any configured baseUrl.

That distinction matters though — image models do honor the configured base URL, including for model listing and connection tests, so that part of the flow isn't fixed. The "开源版" comments suggest this is an open-source fork where certain endpoints stay pinned to aioss.cc while others remain configurable.

Text models are a separate case worth flagging as a side note: their base URL is currently fixed to aioss.cc and any custom address set in settings is silently ignored. That's not directly what the user asked about, but it's the kind of surprising behavior that could explain "some addresses don't work" if they're testing through Agent, 反推, or prompt optimization rather than image generation itself.

I'm also considering whether to pull real evidence from the desktop app's task database to check actual failure error messages, since task_items likely has an error column and this would give concrete proof rather than just code inspection. I'd need to locate dataRoot (probably app.getPath('userData')) and read tasks.sqlite in read-only mode, keeping in mind the running app might have it in WAL mode which usually still permits reads.

+WEB_DB = pathlib.Path(r"F:\项目\nova-image-studio\backend\nova-tasks.sqlite")
+SECRET_FIELDS = {"apiKey", "api_key", "key", "token", "secret", "password"}
+
+
+def ro(path):
+    return sqlite3.connect(path.resolve().as_uri() + "?mode=ro", uri=True)
+
+
+def clip(value, n=260):
+    text = str(value or "").replace("\n", " ").strip()
+    return text if len(text) <= n else text[:n] + " …"
+
+
+def dump_task_db(path):
+    if not path.exists():
+        print(f"(no {path})")
+        return
+    con = ro(path)
+    rows = con.execute(
+        "SELECT id, status, error, created_at, request_json FROM tasks "
+        "WHERE status = 'failed' OR (error IS NOT NULL AND error != '') ORDER BY created_at DESC LIMIT 25"
+    ).fetchall()
+    print(f"\n== {path} : {len(rows)} failed tasks ==")
+    for task_id, status, error, created_at, request_json in rows:
+        req = json.loads(request_json or "{}")
+        print(f"- {created_at} {status} protocol={req.get('protocol')} model={req.get('model')} "

+              f"ratio={req.get('aspectRatio')} custom={req.get('customSize') or '-'} "
+              f"quality={req.get('gptImageQuality')} bg={req.get('gptImageBackground')}")
+        print(f"    task error: {clip(error)}")
+        for idx, item_status, item_error in con.execute(
+            "SELECT item_index, status, error FROM task_items WHERE task_id = ? AND error IS NOT NULL AND error != ''",
+            (task_id,),
+        ):
+            if item_error != error:
+                print(f"    item[{idx}] {item_status}: {clip(item_error)}")
+    con.close()
+
+
+dump_task_db(ROOT / "tasks.sqlite")
+dump_task_db(WEB_DB)
+
+app_db = ROOT / "app.sqlite"
+if app_db.exists():
+    con = ro(app_db)
+    keys = con.execute("SELECT namespace, storage_key, length(value_json) FROM app_settings ORDER BY storage_key").fetchall()
+    print("\n== app_settings keys ==", ", ".join(f"{k}({n})" for _, k, n in keys))
+    for namespace, key, _ in keys:
+        raw = con.execute("SELECT value_json FROM app_settings WHERE namespace = ? AND storage_key = ?", (namespace, key)).fetchone()[0]
+        try:

All show hasApiKey as false in app_settings, but that's just because keys are actually stored separately in encrypted app_secrets, not because keys are missing.

The xianapi.cloud endpoint with gpt-image-2-4k is a likely candidate for failures, though I can't confirm without direct error logs. I now want to compare the actual request format the backend sends to the OpenAI Images API against what a minimal standard request would look like, since the backend likely adds extra fields beyond just model, prompt, and size that a strict OpenAI-compatible relay might reject.

Streaming is enabled by default, so requests always include stream and partial_images flags—but the fallback to non-streaming only triggers on specific error message patterns. If a relay fails differently, like with generic errors, timeouts, or malformed SSE responses that the parser doesn't recognize, there's no fallback path and the task simply fails.

Tracing through the SSE parsing logic, standard OpenAI-format streaming events for image generation should parse correctly since the parser checks for b64_json at multiple nesting levels and skips partial image events appropriately. The bigger issue is that relays might emit non-standard formats that break this parsing. I'm also noting that quality, background, and output_format parameters are always sent with defaults since the advanced params object is always truthy in the request builder.

That test file confirms this forwarding behavior is intentional. Now I'm checking the size calculation logic — for 1K with 16:9 aspect ratio, it rounds to a multiple of 16, giving something like 1824x1024.

I'm noticing there's a size limit config in the code, so the relay's "gpt-image-2" might actually be routing to a different backend that rejects or ignores arbitrary sizes like 3840x2160 for 4K requests, while smaller default sizes like 1024x1024 still work fine.

For 1:1 with 4K, side becomes 3840, and '512' returns undefined for size. Now I'm thinking about how the backend handles the base URL — it strips a trailing `/v1` and always appends `/v1/images/generations`, matching the OpenAI SDK convention where `base_url` ending in `/v1` gets `/images/generations` appended, so `https://host` correctly becomes `https://host/v1/images/generations`.

Testing this against several real provider URLs, I notice many break: paths like `/v1beta/openai`, `/api/v3`, or `/api/paas/v4` end up with a duplicated or wrong version segment, producing a 404 that returns an HTML error page instead of JSON. The user's xianapi.cloud address has no extra path so it's fine, but this logic would fail for other providers they might try. I'm also noting that the response parser only accepts string values from specific fields like `b64_json`, `url`, or `image_url`, either top-level or nested under `result/response/output`.

I'm also not fully certain how the code handles downloading from a returned URL — there's a fetch call around line 488 that likely proxies the download, but if the URL expires quickly or blocks hotlinking, that could be another failure point worth flagging cautiously.

On image-to-image, I'm weighing whether the multipart field naming for multiple reference images (`image` vs `image[]`) could trip up some relays, but I'm not confident enough about OpenAI's actual behavior here to state it firmly, so I'll likely leave this out and stay focused on the things I've actually verified.

I'm also considering parallelCount behavior—whether multiple generation requests run concurrently and could hit relay rate limits causing partial failures—but since I haven't confirmed the concurrency model, I'll skip that too. Similarly, gateway timeouts on long 4K generations are plausible but too generic to call out specifically, so I'm moving toward the text model section where the base URL for text models appears to be hardcoded to a fixed domain.

是 OpenAI 协议，但走的是 Images 接口，而且发出去的请求比标准的最简调用多了几样东西。中转站只要有一项不兼容就会失败。大模型按标准协议写的调用一般是最简版本：不开流式、不带扩展参数、用标准尺寸，所以同样的地址和密钥能成功。

**请求是怎么发的**

请求由本地后端发出，不是浏览器，所以不涉及跨域。生图模型用的是你填的地址：文生图是 `POST {地址}/v1/images/generations`（JSON），图生图是 `POST {地址}/v1/images/edits`（multipart），见 [server.js:1186](backend/server.js:1186)。

**和标准最简调用的差别（按可能性排序）**

1. **默认先走流式。** 第一次请求固定带 `stream: true` 和 `partial_images: 1`，见 [server.js:129](backend/server.js:129) 和 [server.js:1463](backend/server.js:1463)。只有报错文字里同时出现 stream 和"不支持 / unknown"这类字样，才会自动改用非流式重试。中转站返回 500、网关超时，或者返回格式不标准的流式数据，都不会重试，直接失败。我认为这条可能性最大。
2. **总是附带扩展参数。** 不管模型有没有开"高级参数"，后端都会带上 `quality: auto`、`background: auto`、`output_format: png`，见 [server.js:754](backend/server.js:754) 和 [server.js:980](backend/server.js:980)。参数校验严格的中转站会直接返回 400。
3. **尺寸是项目自己算的。** 按比例和清晰度换算，例如 16:9 配 1K 是 1824x1024，16:9 配 4K 是 3840x2160，见 [server.js:869](backend/server.js:869)。如果中转站背后的模型只支持 1024x1024、1536x1024、1024x1536 这几档，就会拒绝或超时。
4. **地址拼接规则不同。** 项目会去掉地址末尾的 `/v1`，再统一加上 `/v1/images/...`，见 [server.js:96](backend/server.js:96)。填 `https://host` 或 `https://host/v1` 都没问题。但如果地址里的版本段不是 `/v1`（比如 `/api/v3`、`/v4`），就会拼成错误路径。OpenAI SDK 的做法是直接在 base_url 后面接 `/images/generations`。
5. **返回解析比较窄。** 只认 `b64_json`、`url`、`image_url` 这三个字段，而且值必须是字符串，见 [server.js:1060](backend/server.js:1060)。如果中转站返回的是 `image_url: {url: ...}`、`result` 里直接放 base64，或者正文里的 Markdown 图片链接，都会报"响应中无图片数据"。

可以按失败卡片上的报错大致判断是哪一条：

| 报错里出现 | 多半是 |
|---|---|
| `上游返回了 HTML 页面而不是 JSON`，或 `API 请求失败: 404` | 地址拼错（第 4 条） |
| `API 请求失败: 400`，并提到 size、quality、background、stream 等 | 参数不兼容（第 1 到 3 条） |
| `响应中无图片数据`，或 `响应 JSON 格式无效: data: ...` | 流式格式不标准，或返回字段不认识（第 1、5 条） |
| `API 请求失败: 5xx`，或超时 | 中转站处理不了流式或大尺寸，也没触发非流式重试（第 1、3 条） |

**本机数据**

本机已经查不到失败记录：后端任务 12 小时后过期，历史里的 21 条都是成功的，所以没法确认你那次具体是哪个原因。你配了 5 个生图模型，其中 4 个走 OpenAI 协议。只有 `gpt-image-2-4k` 用的是第三方地址 `https://www.xianapi.cloud`，其余都是 aioss.cc。密钥是单独加密存的，我没有读。

**另一个发现**

文本模型（Agent、反推提示词、提示词优化）的地址在代码里写死成了 `https://www.aioss.cc`，见 [nova-models.ts:74](frontend/src/lib/nova-models.ts:74) 和 [model-endpoints.ts:41](frontend/src/lib/model-endpoints.ts:41)。设置里填别的地址不会生效。生图模型没有这个问题。

**怎么确认**

最快的办法是把失败卡片上的完整报错发给我。也可以先用那个地址试一次"1K + 1:1"，这时尺寸就是标准的 1024x1024，能排除第 3 条。后端支持用环境变量 `NOVA_IMAGE_STREAM=false` 关掉流式，但界面上没有这个开关。

需要的话我可以把请求改得更兼容：

- 流式请求失败时，一律用非流式再试一次。
- 扩展参数只在开了高级参数、且取值不是 auto 时才发送。
- 地址已经带版本段时，不再强制加 `/v1`。
- 解析兼容 `image_url.url`、`result` 里的 base64 和 Markdown 图片链接。

Both endpoints returned the same results with the API key: GET /v1/models returned 200 with three models listed, and no redirect occurred between the domains. Testing a POST with an empty body returned a 404 error about an unsupported model.

This is telling me the gateway defaults to model "gpt-image-2" when none is specified, and this key's group only supports the 2.5-flare variants. Checking against the registry, none of the configured entries actually use modelId "gpt-image-2.5-flare" -- they use "gpt-image-2" or "gpt-image-2.5" instead, so whatever model the user configured wouldn't match what this key's group actually supports.

I confirmed from workspace-task-service tests that the modelId typed by the user is sent directly as the `model` field in the request, so that part checks out.

Now I need to make my test script mirror the user's actual settings more precisely — since their outputSize and aspectRatio are both "auto," the real project request would omit the `size` field entirely, but my script currently always includes a default size for both test cases. I should adjust the test config so the project case can send without a size parameter to match their exact scenario.

With auto/auto defaults, the project body ends up matching TESTS.project minus the size field, which confirms my approach. Running two real generations will take some time, so I'll launch them in the background with logging and poll for results, keeping in mind this costs actual API calls since the user asked for a real test.

The command will already be captured in the thread log along with the key from the user's message, so that's fine. The earlier probe's 404 response mentioning gpt-image-2 even with an empty body just means the gateway defaulted — not important. I'll do the edit first, then launch the background run in the same turn since the launch depends on the updated script.

Actually there's another angle: the app's default model at www.aioss.cc is gpt-image-2, and the probe showed that model isn't supported by any account for this key. If the user assigned this key to the "GPT Image 2" entry, generation would fail with that exact 404 error. Since keys are stored encrypted, I can't verify which entry uses which key, but a modelId mismatch is a strong candidate explanation for why some addresses fail while others succeed.

I should check the SettingsModal code for how modelId gets edited, whether it's a free-text input or a fixed select. My plan: adjust the script to skip size for project tests when the size env var is empty, then grep for the modelId editing UI, and afterward run the generation test in the background. I'll also summarize the probe results so far: no redirect, the key works on both hosts, but the model list issue remains.

Adding more test variants...

Adding more test variants...

JSON key order doesn't actually matter for these APIs, so I don't need to worry about matching it exactly. Now I want to check how SettingsModal.tsx references modelId, so I'll grep for that pattern with limited context.

The standard call succeeds in 27 seconds with a proper 1024x1024 PNG output, and the project's exact request format (streaming with partial images) also works fine, producing a valid PNG through the event stream. So the protocol itself isn't the issue—the failure is likely a mismatch between the model ID configured in the app's registry (things like "GPT Image 2" or "GPT Image 2.5-free") and what's actually available in this key's group, since none of the registered models match gpt-image-2.5-flare exactly.

The user's default image-generation setting points to modelId gpt-image-2, which under this key returns a 404 "not supported by any configured account in this group" error—matching the app's reported failure. I haven't yet tested what happens with non-auto size settings like 2K/4K resolutions, since the current settings are on auto and don't send explicit sizes; that's worth flagging as an untested case if the user wants further verification.

I should also note that since the API key was pasted directly in chat, it now exists in the conversation history and possibly in terminal/thread logs, so I'd recommend rotating it if there's any concern—though the test scripts and log files themselves mask the key and don't store it directly. I still need to clean up the temporary test files I created in the temp benchmarking folder.

As for the generated PNG outputs, I've already confirmed they're valid via the PNG signature and correct 1024x1024 dimensions, so viewing them directly isn't necessary. The key finding is that the exact protocol the project uses (streaming plus extras) actually works fine with the target model, returning a completed image generation event with the base64 data the parser expects—meaning the compatibility issues I flagged earlier don't actually apply.

The real problem seems to be that the API key's group only supports specific models like gpt-image-2.5-flare and its variants, while the app's configured settings default to "GPT Image 2" with modelId gpt-image-2, which isn't in the supported list at all. That mismatch is likely why the same key and endpoint fail inside the project but succeed when tested with the standard protocol using the correct model name. I still need to verify whether gpt-image-2.5 without the flare suffix is also unsupported, since I've only confirmed the 404 for the bare gpt-image-2 identifier.

The fix would be to add or edit an image model entry in Settings with the OpenAI protocol, the correct endpoint address, and the modelId set precisely to gpt-image-2.5-flare, then select that entry in the generation workbench rather than relying on the default GPT Image 2 preset. I'm also considering mentioning the built-in model check feature in settings that pings /v1/models to verify support before generation.

I'm laying out a small results table comparing the two test requests.

So the actual issue in the app: this key works fine on both domains without redirects, but its group only allows three models—`gpt-image-2.5-flare`, `gpt-image-2.5-flare-cf`, and `gpt-image-2.5-sunburst-cf`. Requesting `gpt-image-2` directly gets rejected by the gateway.

我用 `gpt-image-2.5-flare` 发了两次真实生图请求，都成功了。两次都用从 `server.js` 原样拷出的解析代码验证，结果和应用内的行为一致：

| 请求 | 结果 |
|---|---|
| 标准最简调用（不开流式，size 1024x1024） | 200，28 秒，返回 1024x1024 PNG |
| 和项目一模一样的请求（流式 + `partial_images` + quality/background/output_format，按你现在"自动"的设置不带 size） | 200，20 秒，返回一个 `image_generation.completed` 流式事件，项目能正确取出 1024x1024 PNG |

所以我上次列的那几条（流式、扩展参数、地址拼接）在这个地址上都不是问题。

应用里失败的原因：

- 这把密钥在 `aioss.cc` 和 `www.aioss.cc` 上都能用，也没有重定向。但它的分组只开放了 3 个模型：`gpt-image-2.5-flare`、`gpt-image-2.5-flare-cf` 和 `gpt-image-2.5-sunburst-cf`。
- 探测时网关直接返回了 404：`Model "gpt-image-2" is not supported by any configured account in this group`。`gpt-image-2.5` 也不在这个分组的模型列表里。
- 你在 aioss.cc 上配了 3 个生图模型，模型 ID 都是 `gpt-image-2` 或 `gpt-image-2.5`，生图工作台当前默认选的是"GPT Image 2"。密钥是加密存储的，我看不到它挂在哪个模型上。但只要挂在这几个里的任何一个，请求都会被拒，失败卡片上应该就显示这条 404。大模型能成功，是因为它发的就是你给的 `gpt-image-2.5-flare`。

修改方法：在设置 → 模型配置里新建一个生图模型（或者改现有的一个）。协议选 OpenAI，地址填 `https://aioss.cc`，模型 ID 填 `gpt-image-2.5-flare`（这个输入框可以随便填），填好密钥后，在生图工作台里选中它。保存后可以点「检查模型」再确认一下，它会用这个地址拉取模型列表。

密钥是直接贴在对话里的，会留在这次对话记录中，不放心的话建议在后台换一把新的。测试脚本、日志和两张测试图都在 `%TEMP%\nova-ui-bench`，里面没有保存密钥，看完可以和之前的截图一起删掉。

I confirmed several concrete issues: config reads/writes go through synchronous IPC calls, the model registry decrypts every stored API key on each fetch, capability lookups reload the entire registry every time instead of caching, and some UI components call the display-name helper multiple times per render. I also confirmed the server's global task concurrency is hardcoded to 50.
