Message Type: FINAL_ANSWER
Task name: /root
Sender: /root/settings_audit
Payload:
{"agentPath":"/root/settings_audit","status":{"completed":"I'll start by reading the key files to map the settings and model-config flow.

The shell classifier rejected those commands, so I'll switch to the file tools.

Text-model Base URL forcing shows up in `nova-models.ts:299` and `server.js:2087`, but the grep found no `FIXED_MODEL_BASE_URL` in `model-endpoints.ts`, so that part of the known claim needs checking. I'll read the core library files next.

Confirmed so far: the three text-endpoint builders in `model-endpoints.ts` throw away their `baseUrl` argument, `loadRegistry` parses JSON without a guard, and an empty image Base URL quietly falls back to aioss.cc. Next I'm reading `SettingsModal.tsx` in chunks.

I'll keep going with the audit. Next is the state and handler logic in `SettingsModal.tsx`.

Correction to the known claim: the text-model form (SettingsModal.tsx:766-834) has no Base URL input at all. Only image models get one (695-703). Next I'm checking how "检查模型" resolves models, since it only passes IDs.

`checkModelsAvailability` reads the saved registry (ccode-task-client.ts:206), not the draft the user is editing. The modal only passes IDs, so unsaved models and edited keys never actually get tested. The API key also travels in the query string (line 252). Next I'm reading the backend side of that call.

Backend check confirmed: the text proxy ignores any client `baseUrl` (server.js:2087). The model-list proxy only uses one for image models (2178-2180), and it sends back the upstream status code with no body normalization. Next I'm checking whether keys are stored with tasks or logged, and how the server binds.

The user messages are just placeholders, so I'll keep auditing. Next are the backend helpers, task persistence, the listen host, and the desktop storage layer.

Backend check: keys stay in memory only (`apiKeys` Map at server.js:825, excluded from `request_json` at 793-809). But `HOSTNAME` defaults to `0.0.0.0` (124), and `fetchWithTimeout` defaults to a 30-minute timeout (128, 1318), which covers the model-check proxy too. Next I'm checking desktop storage, backups, and registry listeners.

Web backups appear to include the raw `nova-model-registry`, while desktop strips secrets. Next I'm confirming that, plus the desktop config path and the backend token gate.

Enough evidence collected for most findings. I'll run a few last checks: `sendJson`'s null handling, whether Tabs keeps inactive panels mounted, render-time use of registry helpers, text streaming, and the desktop backup stripping.

Read-only source audit; nothing was built or run. The known claim needs one correction: the text-model form ([SettingsModal.tsx:766](frontend/src/components/SettingsModal.tsx:766)) no longer has a Base URL input. The forcing itself is confirmed. What's left is a `baseUrl` that is stored and sent, but ignored by every layer.

1. Text-model API keys always go to aioss.cc (High, verified). The protocol list offers Claude and Gemini, so users will paste first-party keys, which are then sent to aioss.cc. The only disclosure is helper text. Evidence: [server.js:2087](backend/server.js:2087) hard-codes `FIXED_MODEL_BASE_URL`; the builders at [model-endpoints.ts:35](frontend/src/lib/model-endpoints.ts:35) discard their argument with `void baseUrl`; [nova-models.ts:299](frontend/src/lib/nova-models.ts:299) overwrites the field on load. Fix: support per-model text Base URLs end to end, or drop the field and put a warning beside the key input.

2. Switching preset or blanking the Base URL sends a relay key to aioss.cc (High, verified). Choosing a template overwrites name, model ID, Base URL and limits but keeps the key. An empty Base URL is saved as aioss.cc. Evidence: [SettingsModal.tsx:267](frontend/src/components/SettingsModal.tsx:267) `if (patch.builtinPreset)` resets the fields; [nova-models.ts:276](frontend/src/lib/nova-models.ts:276) `raw.baseUrl || preset.baseUrl || FIXED_MODEL_BASE_URL`. Fix: only fill empty fields, or ask before replacing. Reject an empty Base URL.

3. Outside desktop, the backend is an unauthenticated SSRF proxy (High, verified by reading, not exploited). The server binds 0.0.0.0, and auth only exists when the desktop token is set. The model-list proxy fetches any client-supplied `baseUrl` and returns the response body. Desktop is safe: it uses 127.0.0.1 plus a token ([backend-process.js:30](desktop/backend-process.js:30)). Evidence: [server.js:124](backend/server.js:124); [server.js:244](backend/server.js:244) `if (!DESKTOP_SESSION_TOKEN) return true`; [server.js:2178](backend/server.js:2178). Fix: default to 127.0.0.1, require a token, and block private and link-local targets.

4. Web mode stores and exports keys in plaintext (High, verified). Keys sit as plain JSON in localStorage, and the web backup copies them into the zip unchanged with no warning. Desktop encrypts keys with safeStorage and strips them from backups. Web import also wipes current data without asking. Evidence: [runtime-storage.ts:11](frontend/src/lib/runtime-storage.ts:11) `localStorage.setItem`; [backup-utils.ts:30](frontend/src/lib/backup-utils.ts:30) puts the registry in the export list; [backup-utils.ts:585](frontend/src/lib/backup-utils.ts:585) clears data first; [backup-service.js:112](desktop/storage/backup-service.js:112) `stripRegistrySecrets`. Fix: strip keys by default (include them only on opt-in, with a warning) and confirm before import.

5. "检查模型" tests the saved data, not the form (High, verified). The modal passes draft IDs, but the checker reloads the saved registry. Unsaved models drop out, giving an empty result with no message, and edited keys are tested with their old saved values. Evidence: [SettingsModal.tsx:382](frontend/src/components/SettingsModal.tsx:382) passes IDs only; [ccode-task-client.ts:206](frontend/src/lib/ccode-task-client.ts:206) calls `loadRegistry()`. Fix: pass the draft configs, and explain empty results.

6. The check proves little and reports errors badly (Medium-high, verified). It only looks for the ID in `/v1/models` or `/v1beta/models`. Relays without that endpoint fail when they shouldn't, and a pass doesn't prove generation works. Non-JSON replies become `null` and show up as "404 null" or a raw TypeError. The frontend has no timeout, so it waits on a 30-minute backend default. The key also travels in the query string. Evidence: [ccode-task-client.ts:252](frontend/src/lib/ccode-task-client.ts:252) builds the key into the URL and uses plain `fetch`; [server.js:2201](backend/server.js:2201) sends `null`; [server.js:128](backend/server.js:128) sets the timeout. Fix: send a POST, add a 20 s timeout, write plain-language errors, and add a test-generate action.

7. Closing the dialog silently throws away edits (Medium-high, verified). Nothing tracks unsaved changes, so every close goes through and the next open reloads saved data. Deletes aren't confirmed, "设置已保存" stays on screen after new edits, and preferences save instantly while models need the button. Evidence: [SettingsModal.tsx:550](frontend/src/components/SettingsModal.tsx:550) closes unconditionally; [SettingsModal.tsx:189](frontend/src/components/SettingsModal.tsx:189) reloads on open; [SettingsModal.tsx:362](frontend/src/components/SettingsModal.tsx:362) never clears the success message. Fix: track unsaved changes, confirm on close, add a sticky save bar and confirm deletes.

8. Users with only image models can't save (Medium, verified). Save requires a complete image model and a complete text model, and `hasAnyApiKey` checks both with `&&`. Evidence: [SettingsModal.tsx:335](frontend/src/components/SettingsModal.tsx:335); [settings-storage.ts:31](frontend/src/lib/settings-storage.ts:31). Fix: require one complete model and gate text features separately.

9. Save failures and corrupt data aren't handled (Medium, verified by reading). `persistRegistry` has no try/catch, but desktop throws when OS encryption is unavailable. `loadRegistry` calls `JSON.parse` without a guard, so one corrupt value breaks every caller. Evidence: [secret-store.js:18](desktop/storage/secret-store.js:18) throws; [SettingsModal.tsx:358](frontend/src/components/SettingsModal.tsx:358) calls `saveRegistry` unguarded; [nova-models.ts:375](frontend/src/lib/nova-models.ts:375). Fix: catch the error and show it, and fall back to an empty registry with a notice.

10. Default models change silently and don't change back (Medium, verified). An invalid default jumps to the first complete model, and the image-to-image fallback ignores `maxRefImages`. This check reruns on every keystroke, so briefly clearing the default model's key switches the default to another model for good. Evidence: [nova-models.ts:347](frontend/src/lib/nova-models.ts:347); [SettingsModal.tsx:239](frontend/src/components/SettingsModal.tsx:239). Fix: recheck defaults only on save, require `maxRefImages > 0` for image-to-image, and tell the user when a default changes.

11. Base URL validation gaps (Medium, verified). There's no URL or scheme check. Only a trailing `/v1` is stripped (Google: `/v1beta`) before fixed paths are added. So pasted full endpoints, Google URLs ending in `/v1`, and `/api/v3` relays all break. Evidence: [model-endpoints.ts:17](frontend/src/lib/model-endpoints.ts:17); [server.js:1189](backend/server.js:1189) appends `/v1/images/...`. Fix: parse with `new URL`, require http(s), strip known suffixes and show a preview of the final URL.

12. On desktop, reading the registry blocks the UI (Medium, verified by reading). Each `loadRegistry()` is a synchronous IPC call that decrypts every key, and helpers don't cache it. One `GenerationParamsBar` render can make up to 12 of these calls with GPT Image 2 at a fixed size. The ratio check also looks up the hard-coded ID `'gpt-image-2'`, which never matches the IDs the app generates. Evidence: [preload.js:15](desktop/preload.js:15) `sendSync`; [storage-service.js:86](desktop/storage/storage-service.js:86); [GenerationParamsBar.tsx:60](frontend/src/components/GenerationParamsBar.tsx:60); [model-capabilities.ts:194](frontend/src/lib/model-capabilities.ts:194). Fix: cache the registry, refresh it on `nova-model-registry-updated`, and read keys only when sending a request.

13. Missing relay features (Medium, verified). There's no per-model streaming toggle: text clients always send `stream: true`, and image streaming is one global env setting. There are also no custom headers, per-model timeout, path override, test-generate button, or model export/import/duplicate that leaves keys out. Evidence: [reverse-prompt-client.ts:76](frontend/src/lib/reverse-prompt-client.ts:76); [server.js:129](backend/server.js:129) `NOVA_IMAGE_STREAM`; [server.js:2089](backend/server.js:2089) fixed auth headers. Fix: add optional per-model `stream`, `headers`, `timeoutMs` and `pathOverride`.

14. Settings modal re-renders a lot per keystroke (Low, verified by reading). It's one component of 1,100+ lines with 27 `useState` calls. Every keystroke reruns the defaults check, which does two `JSON.stringify` calls, and rebuilds every dropdown's options. The tabs library unmounts inactive panels, which keeps the cost down. Evidence: [SettingsModal.tsx:243](frontend/src/components/SettingsModal.tsx:243); [SettingsModal.tsx:540](frontend/src/components/SettingsModal.tsx:540). Fix: split the model list, editor and defaults into separate components, use `useReducer`, and memoize the options.

No files were changed. I didn't test runtime behaviour, the 12-call count, or whether the SSRF can be reached."}}

payload.text:
The frontend performance audit ended with a "failed" status after hitting a timeout or length limit, but its intermediate progress log already captured several confirmed findings I can work with — like `useWorkspaceJobs` returning a new object every render and `HistoryJobList` rendering all cards in a day group at once.

I've also confirmed there's no dynamic importing or lazy loading anywhere, only two virtualizer usages, and several heavy libraries are statically imported into a single startup chunk. The server-rendered hidden panel shows placeholder text that client-side stored jobs then overwrite, which is the source of the React #418 hydration mismatch.

The truncated log still had open questions — whether completion blob URLs get revoked, whether the hidden canvas component handles global key/paste events, and some API-key hydration details — so I should do a few targeted checks myself on the highest-value items rather than re-run the whole audit.

I'm planning to check chunk sizes for the startup bundle, trace blob URL revocation on completed jobs, look for global key and paste listeners on the canvas component, and confirm what the virtualizer is actually used for across the codebase.

I also want to check the prompt gallery fetch behavior on mount — whether it hits a remote source even while hidden. Beyond that, I already have enough verified evidence from earlier work: the hydration mismatch on stored jobs, the per-day group virtualization rendering, the saveJobs sync-write path, loadRegistry's sync IPC decrypt cost, and preload/storage-service details, so I don't need to re-verify those.

Since the frontend agent already finished its work, I'll close it and run a few quick parallel checks myself rather than respawning. Next I want to measure chunk sizes in the build output directory, sorted by size, using a PowerShell listing command.

I'll also grep for patterns like createObjectURL and revokeObjectURL across source files, and check CanvasEditor for window/document event listeners that aren't gated by an active or hidden state, possibly using a regex across the canvas components directory with some result limit.

Beyond that, I want to confirm PromptGallery's fetch-on-mount behavior by grepping for useEffect, fetch, and related data-loading calls, plus quickly scan index.html for which chunk scripts load at startup. After those checks, I'll put together the final report in Chinese — covering findings across three categories: performance issues ranked by impact, settings/correctness items, and security concerns.

For the performance section, I'm prioritizing issues most relevant to the user's Windows Electron setup. The biggest win is replacing synchronous config IPC calls with an in-memory registry cache, since `loadRegistry()` currently decrypts every model key through DPAPI on each render — this affects history cards, the params bar, and anything calling that helper, and it's something my earlier benchmarks missed because they used a fake bridge.

Next, `saveJobs` rewrites the entire job list synchronously on every state change, including each polling tick, so I'll switch it to per-record async saves or debounce it. Backend concurrency also defaults to 50, which is too high on desktop given base64 memory overhead — I'll make it configurable. And there's a React #418 hydration mismatch in the image-generation panel on every load, forcing a client re-render, which I've confirmed from both my own benchmark and the static HTML output.

Also flagging that server-rendered placeholder text conflicts with client-side job data, which could be fixed by deferring job reads until after mount or suppressing hydration warnings on those elements — either way it means a startup cost. There's also no lazy loading anywhere: all seven workspaces and heavy libs like gifenc/fflate/jszip/localforage are bundled eagerly into the startup chunk, so switching to dynamic imports for canvas/gif/assets and lazy-loading those libraries would cut initial JS significantly.

Beyond that, virtualization is too coarse since a single day group can contain hundreds of cards rendered at once, so splitting groups into rows would help. The desktop startup also converts every history reference image to a data URL upfront, which should be lazy instead. On the backend side, response bodies get fully buffered in memory and streaming is enabled by default but the partial output just gets thrown away, so turning streaming off by default would make sense given how rarely it's actually used.

Now I'm thinking about the stream fallback behavior. The UI shows a waiting card with a shimmer effect, not progressive image rendering, so there's no visible benefit to streaming here. Turning it off would lower memory pressure and avoid the fragile fallback path, but streaming does help keep connections alive through proxies with idle timeouts during long generations, which is a real trade-off worth noting. The audit also flagged that the fallback only triggers on a narrow regex match, so improving that trigger condition is another item.

Beyond that, there are timeout concerns: the upstream request timeout only covers waiting for headers, so a trickling body could drag on for 30 minutes, and model-check and download requests inherit that same long default when they should have much shorter per-route timeouts (like 20s and 2min). Similarly, shutdown waits up to 8 seconds before killing processes, which risks losing work or leaving WAL files uncheckpointed.

I'm also noting that the text proxy doesn't cancel upstream requests when the user closes the chat, so tokens keep burning in the background. For settings correctness, the text model's baseUrl is essentially ignored and always routes to aioss.cc — the UI hides it, but keys for Claude or Gemini still get sent there, which is a disclosure issue worth flagging to users. And switching presets resets the baseUrl field while leaving the key in place.

Also, the Base URL field has no validation, and saving requires both image and text models configured even if you only use image generation. The "check models" feature tests saved values rather than whatever's currently in the form, uses a query-string key, and has no timeout. Closing without saving silently discards edits, deleting has no confirmation, and default model selection can shift unexpectedly while editing. Corrupted registry JSON breaks everything, and save failures aren't caught. Per-model streaming toggles, custom headers, and timeouts are also missing.

I've verified the security findings myself, confirming the "check models" behavior by reading the actual code. The web backend binds to all interfaces with no auth when no desktop token is set, making the model-list proxy exploitable for SSRF on an exposed Docker deployment — though desktop use is safe since it binds to localhost with a token. Web mode also stores and exports API keys in plaintext, and importing a backup wipes existing data without confirmation.

Now I'm grouping all of this into priority tiers for the fix plan: first, the biggest and safest wins like caching the registry in memory, switching saveJobs to async or debounced writes, lowering concurrency, and fixing the hydration issue.

Second tier covers settings UX and correctness fixes. Third is security, which only matters if the web version is deployed publicly. Fourth addresses bundle size and virtualization, which would take more effort. I'll ask the user which group to tackle first.

I still need to double-check the UI-related claims before presenting them—specifically hasAnyApiKey's logic across its remaining lines—though given limited context budget, I'll just soften the phrasing from "verified" to "per code reading" where appropriate.

Once I confirm those remaining checks, I'll close the perf agent and move toward finalizing the answer. For the chunk size check, I'll list the largest JS files by size and also grab the script references in the main HTML file.

I also want to inspect index.html's script chunk list, since chunk 902 is reportedly loaded at startup. I'll check whether createObjectURL calls have matching revokeObjectURL calls somewhere in the source, keeping an eye on how many turn up.

Next I'm looking for global event listeners in the canvas components folder that might fire while hidden — like keydown or paste handlers — capped to a manageable number of matches, plus checking how PromptGallery loads its data on mount.

I realize I should check more carefully whether the prompt gallery only loads when visible. Given limited remaining budget, I'll run these quick verification checks in parallel, then write the final answer directly without over-analyzing.

The frontend performance review hit its limit before writing its report and has stopped. Its progress log did confirm several things:

- All 7 workspaces are imported statically; nothing uses `next/dynamic` or lazy loading anywhere.
- The whole project has only two lists that use virtualization.
- gifenc, fflate, localforage and jszip are all bundled into chunk 902, which loads at startup.
- The static HTML pre-renders the hidden image-generation panel as "共 0 条". When saved jobs exist, the client renders different text, and that is the cause of the React #418 error.

I'll check the remaining items it didn't finish myself: chunk sizes, whether blob URLs are released, whether the hidden canvas still listens to global keyboard/paste events, and whether the prompt gallery fetches data on startup.

payload.text:
I've gathered enough evidence now, so I'm ready to consolidate the verified findings about bundle size, startup performance, and other optimization opportunities into a final Chinese-language answer.

Bundle size stands out: startup loads roughly 1787KB of JS uncompressed, with heavy chunks tied to library dependencies, and none of the seven workspaces use dynamic imports—they're all statically loaded upfront.

I'm also flagging a lower-confidence issue: the canvas editor's global keyboard/paste listeners might stay active even when the canvas tab is hidden after being opened once, though I haven't confirmed whether there's a proper active-state gate—I'll note this as a suspected, low-priority item to verify rather than a confirmed bug.

Checking the prompt gallery's blacklist fetch and blob URL handling in the image downloader—both seem intentional/minor rather than actual leaks, so I'm skipping them from the verified issues list.

Now I'm compiling my verified findings, starting with the synchronous IPC and per-key decryption happening on every registry load, which I confirmed by tracing calls through the preload script, storage service, and multiple UI components that call getModelDisplayName repeatedly per card render.

I want to flag that my earlier benchmark used a fake localStorage bridge that didn't capture this slowdown, so the real desktop app suffers more here than my initial perf numbers suggested—worth noting since it affects that earlier conclusion.

Next is the full job list rewrite happening synchronously on every job change, which persists through the sync IPC path on desktop—I verified this directly in the job persistence code and the store implementation.

Then there's a hydration mismatch (React error #418) triggered every time jobs exist on load: the static HTML shows an empty state for the hidden image-generation panel, but the client immediately reads storage on mount and discovers actual jobs, forcing React to discard the server-rendered HTML and re-render from scratch. The fix is to defer reading storage until after mount, or only render job-dependent UI once mounted.

I'm also noting the startup bundle is bloated at 1787 KB with no lazy loading across the seven workspaces, and heavy libraries sit directly in the startup chunk — dynamic imports for canvas/gif/prompt-gallery components and lazy-loading heavy compression libraries at their point of use would help.

History virtualization is another issue: a day group with many jobs renders every card at once instead of virtualizing rows, something I confirmed by checking the list component directly.

Now I'm looking at how the desktop app converts stored images on load.

Model list and download endpoints use a 30-minute default timeout, so per-route timeouts need fixing. The text proxy also doesn't cancel upstream requests when the client disconnects, which keeps billing tokens running — a medium concern, along with shutdown behavior deleting interrupted task files on restart and the startup sequence running quick_check on every launch.

On the settings side, text model API keys always get sent to aioss.cc regardless of baseUrl, which I confirmed across model-endpoints.ts, nova-models.ts, and server.js — this is a real privacy disclosure issue since the settings UI no longer even shows a Base URL input for text models. Also, selecting a preset overwrites the name/modelId/baseUrl/limits but keeps the existing key, meaning switching presets on a relay config could send that relay's key to aioss.cc instead.

I'm also verifying that empty baseUrl values fall back to the fixed URL, that saving requires both an image model and text model configured (blocking image-only users), and that the "检查模型" check reads from the saved registry rather than draft edits — so unsaved changes get tested against old values, and the check can produce false negatives for models not listed via /v1/models even when they actually work. I've also noted that closing the settings dialog silently discards edits without confirmation, and there are gaps in Base URL validation still to look at.

Continuing through the remaining issues: defaults silently change on every keystroke, a corrupted registry JSON file (unguarded JSON.parse) would break everything, and several relay features are missing (per-model stream toggle, custom headers, timeout, test-generate). On the security side, the web backend binds to 0.0.0.0 with no auth unless a desktop token is present, and the model-list proxy fetches an arbitrary client-supplied baseUrl, creating an SSRF risk — though the desktop mode itself stays safe since it's bound to localhost with a token. This matters mainly for Docker/web deployments since the project ships a Dockerfile.

Binding to 0.0.0.0 is actually necessary inside Docker for port mapping, so the real fix isn't switching the default host but adding proper access control and SSRF guards on the proxy endpoints — I want to phrase that nuance carefully rather than just saying "default to localhost." I'll also note that web mode stores API keys in plaintext localStorage and includes them in backup zip exports, with import wiping existing data without confirmation, though I haven't personally verified the backup-utils code for this. Finally, there's a desktop-specific performance issue where thumbnails re-decrypt credentials on every render.

I checked the model-capabilities size check that hardcodes 'gpt-image-2' — the agent claimed it never matches generated IDs, but tracing through the fallback logic shows it actually works because the lookup falls back to using the modelId itself as the presetId, so it's harmless aside from an extra registry load; I'll skip flagging this. I also want to briefly mention that my earlier frame-rate benchmarks used a mocked desktop interface and didn't cover this sync IPC path, which is relevant context for how the user should interpret the performance numbers.

Now I'm framing the final answer: lead with the most impactful issues — the desktop app problem, a settings correctness bug where keys go to the wrong place, and a security gap in web deployment — noting everything comes from code reading plus some measurements, without making any actual changes. I'll organize the rest as grouped, proportionally-sized content, keeping in mind the style guidance to favor connected prose over headers, using lists only for genuinely parallel items and tables only for mappings, even though this answer covers a lot of ground.

I'll structure each finding item with title, one-sentence impact, evidence link, and fix, keeping entries to 2-3 lines. I'm organizing findings into groups, starting with performance issues since they affect desktop most, followed by other categories.

I'm grouping the remaining issues: config-related, security concerns for web/Docker deployment, and backend stability items like timeouts and stream fallback. Then I'll propose a phased rollout order — quick low-risk wins first (caching, debounced saves, hydration fixes), followed by lazy loading and virtualization, then security hardening — and ask which batch to tackle first.

I should be upfront about confidence: I'll flag which findings I actually measured myself versus which are based on code reading. The measured ones are the repeated load issue, the startup bundle size, and the missing sunburst data from the API test; everything else comes from reading the code, some of it confirmed personally and some from other agents' notes.

地址覆盖、网页版鉴权缺失这几处我是逐行核对过的，其余判断依赖代理审查的代码阅读结果，这点要说清楚。

至于启动 JS 未压缩体积 1787 KB 这个数字，它是本地文件大小总和，由 Electron 本地加载，所以压缩率的影响不完全等同于网络传输场景。

我打算控制回答长度，列出最关键的几项优化点，次要项（如缩略图解密、启动完整性检查）简单提及即可，不展开细讲。开头用"有，而且有几处比界面样式影响更大"这种直接的语气切入正文。

我先明确哪些点是我逐行核对过的（同步 IPC、整表写入、水合报错、保存限制、检查模型读旧配置、切换模板覆盖地址、网页版无鉴权），剩下的是靠审查代理产出的代码阅读结果，没有逐一复核，得诚实说明这一点。

接下来准备写"性能"这一类下的第一条：桌面端读取模型配置时会卡住界面，因为 `config.get` 走的是同步 IPC，主进程读取模型注册表时要用系统密钥环解每个模型的密钥，这个过程会阻塞。

然后是第二条：任务列表每次变动都会整表重新序列化写入 SQLite，任务多了会越来越慢，建议改成按条异步写入或做防抖处理。

还发现一个真实的水合失败问题：静态 HTML 预渲染时生图面板显示"共 0 条"，但客户端首帧就从存储读出了历史记录，两者文字不一致触发 React #418，导致 React 丢弃预渲染结果、在客户端整棵重建。

没有 Suspense 边界的情况下这会导致整个根节点重新渲染，建议是挂载后再读存储，或者把依赖历史数据的部分延后到挂载后渲染。另外首页启动加载的 JS 体积也偏大，实测要加载 9 个脚本，总计约 1.79MB（未压缩）。

7 个工作区全部是静态导入，全项目没有任何 `next/dynamic` 或懒加载，连 gifenc、fflate、localforage、jszip 这些库都被打进了启动即加载的包里。建议把画布、动图、素材、反推、提示词广场这几个模块改成按需动态加载，编解码库也改成用到时才 import。

历史列表的虚拟化粒度也太粗，只按天虚拟化，同一天的卡片会一次性全部渲染，如果一天生成几百张图就会造成性能问题。

桌面端启动时会把所有历史参考图逐个读文件并转成 base64，历史越多启动越慢、占用内存也越大，应该改成用到时再读取。

后端默认并发上限 50，还默认开启流式响应，却把整个响应体先读进内存再解析，中间预览帧直接丢弃；一张4K图的 base64 大约10–20MB，并发一高内存峰值会很吓人。我在想桌面端可以把并发降到4–8，流式响应要么默认关闭，要么改成边接收边解析。不过流式连接确实能防止代理网关的空闲超时，关掉是否值得还需要权衡。

后端稳定性上还有几个问题：超时机制只覆盖等待响应头，头一到就清掉计时器，之后全靠30分钟的全局空闲超时兜底，模型列表和图片下载也共用这个超时，应该按接口分别设置更合理的上限，比如模型列表20秒、下载2分钟。文本代理关闭对话后也不会取消上游请求，上游流还在继续跑、继续计费。流式失败后只有报错文字命中特定正则才会回退非流式，而且错误信息里带timeout/abort字样就统一显示成笼统提示，原始状态码全丢了。退出时若有任务进行中，会等8秒强杀后端，这些细节都需要理清楚。

设置方面还有问题：文本模型的密钥一律发往固定地址，即便协议里提供其他模型选项、用户填了官方密钥，也会被转发过去，需要明确提示或支持真正的自定义地址。切换内置模板时会覆盖名称、模型ID、地址和上限但保留密钥，地址留空保存时又会自动回填默认地址，这样密钥可能被错误发送，应该只填空字段或先确认、地址为空时报错。

只用生图功能也强制要求配文本模型才能保存，这个限制不太合理。「检查模型」读取的是已保存配置而非编辑中的内容，没保存的模型不会被检查，改过密钥测的还是旧的；而且它只检查模型名是否在列表里，像某些能用但未列出的模型会被误报，应该检查草稿内容、加超时、再加"试生成"按钮验证实际可用性。

关闭设置窗口时未保存的修改会直接丢弃，删除模型也没有确认提示。

模型注册表 JSON 损坏时 loadRegistry 会直接抛错，导致所有调用处一起挂掉，保存失败也没有做异常捕获。此外，中转站常用的选项都缺失：按模型开关流式、自定义请求头、超时设置。

安全方面，后端没有鉴权，只有桌面端设置了会话令牌时才校验，这意味着网页或 Docker 部署下任何能访问该端口的人都能直接使用。

更严重的是，模型列表代理会请求客户端给出的任意地址并把结果原样返回，这可能被当作跳板去探测内网。Docker 部署因为需要监听 0.0.0.0，风险更突出，关键要加访问控制并禁止代理访问内网和本机地址；桌面端只监听 127.0.0.1 且带令牌，不受影响。另外网页版密钥是明文存在 localStorage 里，备份时也会把密钥原样打进 zip，导入备份还会先清空现有数据而不做确认；桌面端密钥则是系统加密存储，备份时会剔除密钥。

最后按改动大小和收益排了个优先级：第一批是注册表缓存、任务异步写入、水合、并发数调整，以及几个设置项；第二批是按需加载、按行虚拟化、后端的超时/取消/回退/退出处理；第三批是剩下的部分。

我还想标注一下哪些结论是我自己验证过的，哪些是其他 agent 报告但我没亲自核实的，避免混淆确定性程度。有几个次要问题（S3 缩略图重复解密、启动时的完整性检查、窗口创建时机）打算作为附带说明一笔带过，不深入展开。最后打算问用户想从哪一批开始改。

Checking the SSRF-related code around line 2178-2199, I see it confirms that for image type models, the client-supplied baseUrl gets used in the fetch call — that's enough to support the claim. As for #12 (that text model forms no longer have a Base URL field), that's something I picked up from the settings agent's review, not something I personally verified in the form itself.

I should correct my earlier statement about custom addresses not taking effect — the accurate picture is that there's no input field for that at all now, which changes the framing slightly but leads to the same overall conclusion that the address is fixed. I'll fold in that correction naturally rather than dwelling on it, and expect the final answer to run fairly long given the user wants a comprehensive review.

   - 建议：在内存里缓存一份注册表，保存或收到 `nova-model-registry-updated` 时刷新；密钥只在真正发请求时再读取。
2. **任务每变一次，整张任务表都要同步重写一遍。**

3. **每次启动都会有一次水合失败（实测）。**
   - 原因：静态 HTML 里预渲染的生图面板显示"共 0 条"，而客户端第一帧就从存储里读出了历史（`useState(loadInitialJobs)`，[useWorkspaceJobs.ts:31](frontend/src/hooks/useWorkspaceJobs.ts:31)）。两边文字对不上，React 抛出 #418，丢掉预渲染结果，改在客户端重新渲染。
   - 建议：挂载完成后再读存储，或者只在挂载后渲染依赖历史数据的部分。
4. **启动时加载的 JS 偏大（实测）。**
   - 现状：首页启动要加载 9 个脚本，共约 1.79MB（未压缩），其中 page 包就有 721KB。7 个工作区全是静态导入，整个项目没有一处 `next/dynamic`；gifenc、fflate、localforage 和 jszip 也打进了启动就会加载的 902 包（399KB）。

5. **历史列表的虚拟化粒度太粗。** 现在按"天"分组做虚拟化，同一天的卡片会一次全部渲染（[HistoryJobList.tsx:461](frontend/src/components/workspace/results/HistoryJobList.tsx:461)）。一天生成几百张，就会一次挂上几百张卡片。建议改成按行虚拟化。
6. **桌面端启动时，会把所有历史参考图都转成 data URL**（[job-store.ts:172](frontend/src/lib/job-store.ts:172)）：逐个读文件再做 base64 编码，历史越多，启动越慢、内存占用越高。建议等用到时再读。
7. **后端并发和内存。**
   - 现状：默认最多 50 个任务同时跑（[server.js:23](backend/server.js:23)）。流式请求默认开启，但后端会把整个响应读进内存才解析，中间的预览帧直接丢掉（[server.js:1143](backend/server.js:1143)）。一张 4K 图的 base64 约 10–20MB，并发一高，内存峰值就很大。

**后端稳定性**

9. **文本代理不会取消上游请求。** 关掉对话后，上游的流还在继续跑、继续计费（[server.js:2140](backend/server.js:2140)）。
10. **流式失败后的回退太窄。** 只有报错文字命中特定正则时才回退到非流式（[server.js:1471](backend/server.js:1471)）。另外，报错里只要带 timeout 或 abort，就一律显示成"请求超时"或"网络连接失败"，原始状态码丢失。
11. **退出时的处理。** 有任务在跑时退出，会等 8 秒后强制结束后端（[backend-process.js:111](desktop/backend-process.js:111)）；下次启动时，中断任务里已经生成好的图片也会被一起删掉。

**设置**

12. **文本模型的密钥一律发往 aioss.cc**（[model-endpoints.ts:35](frontend/src/lib/model-endpoints.ts:35)、[server.js:2087](backend/server.js:2087)）。修正我上次的说法：文本模型表单里现在根本没有 Base URL 输入框，不是"填了不生效"。但协议里有 Claude、Gemini 等选项，用户填官方密钥，也会被发到 aioss.cc。建议：要么真正支持每个模型自定义地址，要么在密钥输入框旁边写清楚这一点。
13. **切换内置模板会覆盖掉原来的配置。** 名称、模型 ID、地址和各项上限都会被重置，但密钥保留（[SettingsModal.tsx:267](frontend/src/components/SettingsModal.tsx:267)）。地址留空保存时，会自动变成 aioss.cc（[nova-models.ts:276](frontend/src/lib/nova-models.ts:276)）。结果是中转站的密钥可能被发到 aioss.cc。建议：模板只填空着的字段，或者覆盖前先确认；地址为空时直接报错。
14. **只用生图也必须配一个文本模型才能保存**（[SettingsModal.tsx:334](frontend/src/components/SettingsModal.tsx:334)）。
15. **「检查模型」读的是已保存的配置，不是正在编辑的内容**（[ccode-task-client.ts:206](frontend/src/lib/ccode-task-client.ts:206)）。没保存的模型不会被检查，改过的密钥测的还是旧的。它也只看模型名在不在 `/v1/models` 列表里，所以像 `gpt-image-2.5-sunburst` 这种实际能用、但不在列表里的模型会被误报。建议：检查正在编辑的内容，加上超时，再加一个"试生成"按钮。
16. **其他问题：**
    - 关掉设置窗口时，未保存的修改会被直接丢弃；删除模型也没有确认。
    - 注册表数据损坏时，`loadRegistry` 会直接抛错，所有调用它的地方一起出错（[nova-models.ts:375](frontend/src/lib/nova-models.ts:375)）。
    - 保存失败时没有捕获错误，也没有提示。
17. **缺少中转站常用的选项**：按模型开关流式、自定义请求头、单独设置超时。

**安全（只影响网页 / Docker 部署）**

18. **后端没有鉴权。**
    - 现状：只有桌面端设置了会话令牌时才校验（[server.js:243](backend/server.js:243)）。网页或 Docker 部署时，任何能访问端口的人都能用它发任务。模型列表代理会请求客户端给出的任意地址，并把结果原样返回（[server.js:2178](backend/server.js:2178)），可能被当成跳板去访问内网。
    - 建议：Docker 里必须监听 0.0.0.0，所以关键在加访问控制，并禁止代理访问内网和本机地址。桌面端只监听 127.0.0.1 并带令牌，不受影响。
19. **网页版的密钥和备份。** 网页版的密钥明文存在 localStorage，备份时会原样打进 zip（[backup-utils.ts:30](frontend/src/lib/backup-utils.ts:30)）；导入备份会先清空现有数据，不做确认。桌面端的密钥由系统加密存储，备份时也会去掉。

建议分三批处理：

- 第一批：改动小、收益大，第 1、2、3、7、13、14、15 条。
- 第二批：按需加载、按行虚拟化，加上后端的超时、取消、回退和退出，即第 4、5、8–11 条。
- 第三批：准备部署网页版时再做，第 18、19 条。

This is a broad analysis request asking me to identify optimization opportunities across the project, so I should focus on investigating and proposing rather than implementing changes. Given the scope, it might be worth delegating the deeper codebase investigation to a sub-agent to keep my main context free for any follow-up implementation work.

I'm already recalling relevant findings from earlier in this session that I can report with evidence — like the settings UI letting users configure a text model base URL that's actually ignored, since the server hardcodes it to a fixed URL regardless of what's configured, which makes that setting misleading. I'm also noting that the backend always sends quality, background, and output format parameters unconditionally, which is another area worth flagging for optimization.

There's also a real hydration bug I want to verify: React #418 hydration mismatch errors occurring on every load, likely because a hook reads localStorage during initial render (loading stored jobs and checking for API keys before mount), causing the server-rendered HTML to not match the client render. This forces React to discard and re-render the whole tree client-side, which costs real startup time — worth confirming and reporting since every benchmarked scenario showed this exception.

saveJobs writes the entire jobs array to storage on every change, stringifying synchronously inside the state updater — that's blocking work that scales with job history size, plus a redundant save-on-mount effect. I'm also noting the desktop IPC path for config.set is unclear whether it's synchronous, which could add latency.

Beyond that, I found a bigger issue: loadStoredImages pulls every stored image record (full base64 strings) from IndexedDB into memory at startup and attaches them to every job in state. With hundreds of generated high-resolution images each several MB in base64, this means startup loads potentially gigabytes into memory at once — a real perf bottleneck.

Though newer code paths might store blob references instead of raw base64 via image-downloader's stored blob refs, resolved lazily by getImageSrc, so this concern may only apply to older jobs that still have inline base64 data rather than refs.

Actually digging deeper, I see desktop's job-store list function loads every history record at startup and converts each reference image to a data URL via disk reads and base64 encoding for ALL records upfront — this is a genuine startup perf issue since it scales as jobs times ref-images-per-job, all done eagerly via IPC. I can flag this with solid evidence from job-store.ts.

On the backend, I'm looking at how task ref images and API keys get held in memory maps until tasks complete, plus how result images get stored.

Then I check that images are stored as base64 text in sqlite with a 12-hour TTL cleanup — that seems reasonable.

For the settings modal, it's a large 63KB component, but I suspect Base UI's Dialog unmounts its content when closed by default, so it's probably fine unless keepMounted is explicitly set.

More concerning is that all six or seven workspace tabs — agent, image-gen, canvas, assets, reverse prompt, gif, prompt gallery — appear to be kept mounted simultaneously, which means they all pay initial render cost and memory overhead, and hidden tabs keep running effects like polling and subscriptions in the background.

I want to check whether the heavy CanvasEditor and PromptGallery components are truly lazy or eagerly mounted at startup, since PromptGallery might fetch remote prompt sources even if the user never opens it, while AssetsWorkspace and HistoryJobList seem to use active/shouldRender props more carefully. There's also no code splitting via next/dynamic for heavy editors like CanvasEditor, GifFrameTuner, the image annotation editor, or libraries like react-markdown, jszip, gifenc, and fflate — all bundled into one route without lazy-loading.

Fonts and the PWA service worker setup look fine. In Electron, the dark background color avoids a light/dark flash since the window waits until ready-to-show, and the sandboxed child process backend seems fine too.

For settings, I'm noting several issues: the Base URL field for text models appears to be ignored, API keys are stored encrypted on desktop but in plaintext localStorage on web (typical for a web app but worth flagging), and there's room to improve settings UX with key visibility toggles, per-model connection testing, import/export, and Base URL validation warnings for unusual paths.

I also notice WebSocket reconnection uses proper exponential backoff, and queue-status polling runs every 30 seconds as expected. But I'm spotting a real virtualization issue in HistoryJobList: day groups render all cards inside a single day at once without further virtualization, so a day with 100 generated images would render 100 heavy cards simultaneously, which could hurt performance.

I should suggest chunking day groups into rows for proper virtualization instead. Then I want to check a few more areas: whether blob URLs created from IndexedDB blobs get revoked (potential leak), whether the agent chat message list is virtualized for long conversations with images, and whether PromptGallery and AssetsWorkspace's asset grids handle virtualization for large lists.

Given the scope, I'm planning to split this into parallel subagent investigations — one focused on frontend runtime performance (rendering, virtualization, lazy loading, blob URL lifecycle, storage read/write frequency, startup work, hydration issues, and bundle size), and another focused on settings and model configuration issues like the ignored Base URL, validation logic, and secrets handling differences between web and desktop.

For a third area, I want to look at backend and desktop concerns: task queue concurrency, memory usage from base64 image data, WebSocket broadcast frequency, request timeouts, Electron IPC calls that might block the renderer synchronously, and database query patterns that reload all records repeatedly.

I'll delegate these investigations to subagents given the broad scope, then synthesize findings myself with prioritized, evidence-backed recommendations grouped by category, and ask the user which fixes to implement rather than jumping straight into changes.

Actually, I'll just handle the sendSync grep myself quickly alongside the chunk size check, keeping my own tasks light while subagents handle the rest. I'll draft the subagent prompts in English since that's fine internally.

I want subagents to report concise English findings with file:line evidence, capped around 25, ranked by impact, distinguishing verified vs suspected issues, without making any code changes. I'll give them context on the project structure — F:\项目\nova-image-studio with a Next.js frontend, Node backend, and Electron desktop app — and tell them to skip release and cache directories.

I should share what I've already found, like the React #418 error on load and history virtualization, so they don't duplicate work, and remind them this is a Windows PowerShell environment where they should stay read-only, avoiding builds but allowed to run inspection commands.

Now I'm drafting the first audit prompt, focused on frontend runtime performance in the Next.js app, specifying the read-only constraints and pointing them to the entry point at page.tsx and WorkspaceShell.

I want the prompt to direct attention to hidden but mounted tabs still doing background work (effects, timers, polling, observers) and heavy components loaded eagerly like CanvasEditor and PromptGallery, plus which long lists lack virtualization.

Also checking whether history job lists, agent messages, assets grid, prompt gallery, and S3 browser are properly virtualized -- history is virtualized per day group but each group renders all its cards, which could be a worst-case concern. I also want to flag re-render hotspots: state held high in WorkspaceShell (like checkingJobIds/cooldowns Maps and toasts) passed down as props to large lists, and missing memoization on card components.

Beyond that, I'm digging into memory handling — base64 images kept in React state, images loaded eagerly at startup, blob URL creation/revocation patterns, and synchronous localStorage writes on every job update. I want to nail down the exact cause of the React hydration error #418 that fires whenever jobs exist, likely from useState initializers reading storage during first render. And I should measure the biggest JS chunks in the build output to spot modules like the canvas editor, gif tools, or heavy libraries that could be lazy-loaded with next/dynamic. The end goal is a ranked list of the most impactful fixes.

Now I'm shifting to drafting a similar audit prompt for the settings and model-configuration feature, pointing at the key files that handle the settings modal, model registry, endpoints, and storage.

I want the audit to confirm or refine what's already suspected: that text models' Base URL is hardcoded to a fixed endpoint across the normalization logic, model-endpoints, and the server, rather than just restating it.

Beyond that, I'm hunting for real, evidence-backed issues -- like the UI showing fields that are actually ignored, preset selection silently overwriting user-entered values for image models, missing validation on Base URL formatting or trailing paths, empty API keys slipping through, and what the "check models" feature actually verifies versus what it can't prove.

I'm also thinking through security: whether keys sit in plaintext localStorage on web versus encrypted storage on desktop, whether they ever hit the backend or get logged, and whether exports/backups leak them. On top of that, I want to look at performance costs in the settings UI -- re-renders per keystroke, expensive work triggered on open/save like registry update events or synchronous IPC calls.

Then I'm drafting the specification for a separate audit prompt targeting the backend and desktop shell, focused on performance, resource, and reliability issues, explicitly read-only and excluding build artifacts, node_modules, and temp/release directories.

Also desktop/preload.js, ipc.js, backend-process.js, and the storage/S3 modules to check. I want to find evidence-backed issues like whether config get/set is blocking the renderer synchronously, how heavily runtime-storage.ts calls into it across job-store and settings, and whether records.list or files.read are pulling entire datasets over IPC at once.

I'm also looking at memory pressure from base64 images cached in maps and stored as sqlite TEXT, full response bodies being buffered for multi-MB images, JSON.stringify of large payloads, WebSocket broadcast frequency, cleanup timers, concurrency limits, and what happens to in-flight tasks on shutdown. On the reliability side I'm checking the 30-minute request timeout, undici agent settings, and whether stream fallback only triggers on a narrow error pattern match.

I'm planning to spawn explorer sub-agents to audit frontend performance and settings, keeping the final report ranked by impact, capped at 15 findings with file:line evidence, concrete fixes, and confidence labels, all under 900 words.

While waiting on results, I'll avoid duplicating work another subagent is already covering, and once findings come back I'll spot-check the highest-impact claims myself before reporting them as verified.

这次是分析性的问题，我先做全面排查，不直接改代码。范围比较大，我分三路并行只读审查：

- **前端运行时性能**：隐藏标签页仍在后台运行的工作、长列表虚拟化、重复渲染、内存占用、启动开销、打包体积。
- **设置和模型配置**：界面上显示但不生效的字段、校验、密钥存储、设置页本身的性能。
- **后端和桌面端**：同步 IPC、任务队列内存、超时与回退、启动流程。

本次会话已经确认的几条（每次加载都会出现的 React #418 水合报错、历史列表按天分组虚拟化、文本模型地址被写死）会交给各路去核实细节，不重复排查。

I'm tracking three parallel audits I spawned: the backend/desktop one finished and I've been double-checking its findings, while the frontend performance and settings audits are still running.

I confirmed several concrete issues: config reads/writes go through synchronous IPC calls, the model registry decrypts every stored API key on each fetch, capability lookups reload the entire registry every time instead of caching, and some UI components call the display-name helper multiple times per render. I also confirmed the server's global task concurrency is hardcoded to 50.

Now I want to verify whether that display-name helper itself triggers a registry reload, since I haven't actually seen its implementation yet — I need to trace how it's wired to the registry-loading logic in both desktop and web runtime modes.

Estimating the real-world cost: with several visible job cards each calling the display-name helper twice, and each call potentially decrypting multiple stored API keys via native OS decryption plus a synchronous IPC round trip, a single list render could add up to noticeable delay — tens to hundreds of milliseconds — especially since this runs on every re-render, including search typing. This matters because the user is running the Windows desktop build where this overhead is real, unlike my benchmark environment which used a fake bridge with plain in-memory storage and no encryption or IPC overhead, meaning my test wouldn't have captured this slowdown at all.

I also want to double check saveJobs — I confirmed earlier it's invoked inside the state updater in useWorkspaceJobs, which routes through the desktop config setter, triggers a synchronous IPC call, and results in the main process stringifying and writing to SQLite. Since the value passed in is already a JSON string, it gets double-encoded, which is harmless but worth noting, and now I want to check how often this save path actually fires during a single generation.

Each server task poll or WebSocket status update calls the job replace function, which triggers a full-list synchronous write. At the user's current 21-job count, the payload is around 14KB, which is manageable, but it scales linearly — with hundreds of jobs this becomes hundreds of KB written synchronously, so the impact grows meaningfully.

Now I want to wait on the other two agents while I verify getModelDisplayName in parallel. I should stay disciplined here since I hit a token-limit truncation earlier from over-long reasoning, so I'll keep this focused: grep for the getModelDisplayName definition and other hot loadRegistry callers to fully substantiate that claim, then run WaitAgent for the remaining two agents.

The four key claims I checked hold up:

- `config.get/set` go through synchronous `ipcRenderer.sendSync` ([preload.js:15](desktop/preload.js:15)).
- Every read of the model registry has the main process decrypt every model's key ([storage-service.js:86](desktop/storage/storage-service.js:86)).
- The capability checks call `loadRegistry()` each time ([model-capabilities.ts:31](frontend/src/lib/model-capabilities.ts:31)).
- Backend concurrency is capped at 50 by default ([server.js:23](backend/server.js:23)).

One more point: every history card calls `getModelDisplayName` twice. Before counting that against performance, I need to confirm this function also goes through `loadRegistry()`. My earlier benchmark stubbed the desktop bridge with an in-process localStorage, so it didn't catch this synchronous IPC plus decryption cost at all; the real Electron app will be slower on this path than my measurements showed. I'll confirm it while waiting for the other two reviews.

Fix: recheck defaults only on save, require `maxRefImages > 0` for image-to-image, and tell the user when a default changes.

11. Base URL validation gaps (Medium, verified). There's no URL or scheme check. Only a trailing `/v1` is stripped (Google: `/v1beta`) before fixed paths are added. So pasted full endpoints, Google URLs ending in `/v1`, and `/api/v3` relays all break. Evidence: [model-endpoints.ts:17](frontend/src/lib/model-endpoints.ts:17); [server.js:1189](backend/server.js:1189) appends `/v1/images/...`. Fix: parse with `new URL`, require http(s), strip known suffixes and show a preview of the final URL.

12. On desktop, reading the registry blocks the UI (Medium, verified by reading). Each `loadRegistry()` is a synchronous IPC call that decrypts every key, and helpers don't cache it. One `GenerationParamsBar` render can make up to 12 of these calls with GPT Image 2 at a fixed size. The ratio check also looks up the hard-coded ID `'gpt-image-2'`, which never matches the IDs the app generates. Evidence: [preload.js:15](desktop/preload.js:15) `sendSync`; [storage-service.js:86](desktop/storage/storage-service.js:86); [GenerationParamsBar.tsx:60](frontend/src/components/GenerationParamsBar.tsx:60); [model-capabilities.ts:194](frontend/src/lib/model-capabilities.ts:194). Fix: cache the registry, refresh it on `nova-model-registry-updated`, and read keys only when sending a request.

13. Missing relay features (Medium, verified). There's no per-model streaming toggle: text clients always send `stream: true`, and image streaming is one global env setting. There are also no custom headers, per-model timeout, path override, test-generate button, or model export/import/duplicate that leaves keys out. Evidence: [reverse-prompt-client.ts:76](frontend/src/lib/reverse-prompt-client.ts:76); [server.js:129](backend/server.js:129) `NOVA_IMAGE_STREAM`; [server.js:2089](backend/server.js:2089) fixed auth headers. Fix: add optional per-model `stream`, `headers`, `timeoutMs` and `pathOverride`.

14. Settings modal re-renders a lot per keystroke (Low, verified by reading). It's one component of 1,100+ lines with 27 `useState` calls. Every keystroke reruns the defaults check, which does two `JSON.stringify` calls, and rebuilds every dropdown's options. The tabs library unmounts inactive panels, which keeps the cost down. Evidence: [SettingsModal.tsx:243](frontend/src/components/SettingsModal.tsx:243); [SettingsModal.tsx:540](frontend/src/components/SettingsModal.tsx:540). Fix: split the model list, editor and defaults into separate components, use `useReducer`, and memoize the options.

No files were changed. I didn't test runtime behaviour, the 12-call count, or whether the SSRF can be reached."}}

payload.text:
The frontend performance audit ended with a "failed" status after hitting a timeout or length limit, but its intermediate progress log already captured several confirmed findings I can work with — like `useWorkspaceJobs` returning a new object every render and `HistoryJobList` rendering all cards in a day group at once.

I've also confirmed there's no dynamic importing or lazy loading anywhere, only two virtualizer usages, and several heavy libraries are statically imported into a single startup chunk. The server-rendered hidden panel shows placeholder text that client-side stored jobs then overwrite, which is the source of the React #418 hydration mismatch.

The truncated log still had open questions — whether completion blob URLs get revoked, whether the hidden canvas component handles global key/paste events, and some API-key hydration details — so I should do a few targeted checks myself on the highest-value items rather than re-run the whole audit.

I'm planning to check chunk sizes for the startup bundle, trace blob URL revocation on completed jobs, look for global key and paste listeners on the canvas component, and confirm what the virtualizer is actually used for across the codebase.

I also want to check the prompt gallery fetch behavior on mount — whether it hits a remote source even while hidden. Beyond that, I already have enough verified evidence from earlier work: the hydration mismatch on stored jobs, the per-day group virtualization rendering, the saveJobs sync-write path, loadRegistry's sync IPC decrypt cost, and preload/storage-service details, so I don't need to re-verify those.

Since the frontend agent already finished its work, I'll close it and run a few quick parallel checks myself rather than respawning. Next I want to measure chunk sizes in the build output directory, sorted by size, using a PowerShell listing command.

I'll also grep for patterns like createObjectURL and revokeObjectURL across source files, and check CanvasEditor for window/document event listeners that aren't gated by an active or hidden state, possibly using a regex across the canvas components directory with some result limit.

Beyond that, I want to confirm PromptGallery's fetch-on-mount behavior by grepping for useEffect, fetch, and related data-loading calls, plus quickly scan index.html for which chunk scripts load at startup. After those checks, I'll put together the final report in Chinese — covering findings across three categories: performance issues ranked by impact, settings/correctness items, and security concerns.

For the performance section, I'm prioritizing issues most relevant to the user's Windows Electron setup. The biggest win is replacing synchronous config IPC calls with an in-memory registry cache, since `loadRegistry()` currently decrypts every model key through DPAPI on each render — this affects history cards, the params bar, and anything calling that helper, and it's something my earlier benchmarks missed because they used a fake bridge.

Next, `saveJobs` rewrites the entire job list synchronously on every state change, including each polling tick, so I'll switch it to per-record async saves or debounce it. Backend concurrency also defaults to 50, which is too high on desktop given base64 memory overhead — I'll make it configurable. And there's a React #418 hydration mismatch in the image-generation panel on every load, forcing a client re-render, which I've confirmed from both my own benchmark and the static HTML output.

Also flagging that server-rendered placeholder text conflicts with client-side job data, which could be fixed by deferring job reads until after mount or suppressing hydration warnings on those elements — either way it means a startup cost. There's also no lazy loading anywhere: all seven workspaces and heavy libs like gifenc/fflate/jszip/localforage are bundled eagerly into the startup chunk, so switching to dynamic imports for canvas/gif/assets and lazy-loading those libraries would cut initial JS significantly.

Beyond that, virtualization is too coarse since a single day group can contain hundreds of cards rendered at once, so splitting groups into rows would help. The desktop startup also converts every history reference image to a data URL upfront, which should be lazy instead. On the backend side, response bodies get fully buffered in memory and streaming is enabled by default but the partial output just gets thrown away, so turning streaming off by default would make sense given how rarely it's actually used.

Now I'm thinking about the stream fallback behavior. The UI shows a waiting card with a shimmer effect, not progressive image rendering, so there's no visible benefit to streaming here. Turning it off would lower memory pressure and avoid the fragile fallback path, but streaming does help keep connections alive through proxies with idle timeouts during long generations, which is a real trade-off worth noting. The audit also flagged that the fallback only triggers on a narrow regex match, so improving that trigger condition is another item.

Beyond that, there are timeout concerns: the upstream request timeout only covers waiting for headers, so a trickling body could drag on for 30 minutes, and model-check and download requests inherit that same long default when they should have much shorter per-route timeouts (like 20s and 2min). Similarly, shutdown waits up to 8 seconds before killing processes, which risks losing work or leaving WAL files uncheckpointed.

I'm also noting that the text proxy doesn't cancel upstream requests when the user closes the chat, so tokens keep burning in the background. For settings correctness, the text model's baseUrl is essentially ignored and always routes to aioss.cc — the UI hides it, but keys for Claude or Gemini still get sent there, which is a disclosure issue worth flagging to users. And switching presets resets the baseUrl field while leaving the key in place.

Also, the Base URL field has no validation, and saving requires both image and text models configured even if you only use image generation. The "check models" feature tests saved values rather than whatever's currently in the form, uses a query-string key, and has no timeout. Closing without saving silently discards edits, deleting has no confirmation, and default model selection can shift unexpectedly while editing. Corrupted registry JSON breaks everything, and save failures aren't caught. Per-model streaming toggles, custom headers, and timeouts are also missing.

I've verified the security findings myself, confirming the "check models" behavior by reading the actual code. The web backend binds to all interfaces with no auth when no desktop token is set, making the model-list proxy exploitable for SSRF on an exposed Docker deployment — though desktop use is safe since it binds to localhost with a token. Web mode also stores and exports API keys in plaintext, and importing a backup wipes existing data without confirmation.

Now I'm grouping all of this into priority tiers for the fix plan: first, the biggest and safest wins like caching the registry in memory, switching saveJobs to async or debounced writes, lowering concurrency, and fixing the hydration issue.

Second tier covers settings UX and correctness fixes. Third is security, which only matters if the web version is deployed publicly. Fourth addresses bundle size and virtualization, which would take more effort. I'll ask the user which group to tackle first.

I still need to double-check the UI-related claims before presenting them—specifically hasAnyApiKey's logic across its remaining lines—though given limited context budget, I'll just soften the phrasing from "verified" to "per code reading" where appropriate.

Once I confirm those remaining checks, I'll close the perf agent and move toward finalizing the answer. For the chunk size check, I'll list the largest JS files by size and also grab the script references in the main HTML file.

I also want to inspect index.html's script chunk list, since chunk 902 is reportedly loaded at startup. I'll check whether createObjectURL calls have matching revokeObjectURL calls somewhere in the source, keeping an eye on how many turn up.

Next I'm looking for global event listeners in the canvas components folder that might fire while hidden — like keydown or paste handlers — capped to a manageable number of matches, plus checking how PromptGallery loads its data on mount.

I realize I should check more carefully whether the prompt gallery only loads when visible. Given limited remaining budget, I'll run these quick verification checks in parallel, then write the final answer directly without over-analyzing.

The frontend performance review hit its limit before writing its report and has stopped. Its progress log did confirm several things:

- All 7 workspaces are imported statically; nothing uses `next/dynamic` or lazy loading anywhere.
- The whole project has only two lists that use virtualization.
- gifenc, fflate, localforage and jszip are all bundled into chunk 902, which loads at startup.
- The static HTML pre-renders the hidden image-generation panel as "共 0 条". When saved jobs exist, the client renders different text, and that is the cause of the React #418 error.

I'll check the remaining items it didn't finish myself: chunk sizes, whether blob URLs are released, whether the hidden canvas still listens to global keyboard/paste events, and whether the prompt gallery fetches data on startup.

payload.text:
I've gathered enough evidence now, so I'm ready to consolidate the verified findings about bundle size, startup performance, and other optimization opportunities into a final Chinese-language answer.

Bundle size stands out: startup loads roughly 1787KB of JS uncompressed, with heavy chunks tied to library dependencies, and none of the seven workspaces use dynamic imports—they're all statically loaded upfront.

I'm also flagging a lower-confidence issue: the canvas editor's global keyboard/paste listeners might stay active even when the canvas tab is hidden after being opened once, though I haven't confirmed whether there's a proper active-state gate—I'll note this as a suspected, low-priority item to verify rather than a confirmed bug.

Checking the prompt gallery's blacklist fetch and blob URL handling in the image downloader—both seem intentional/minor rather than actual leaks, so I'm skipping them from the verified issues list.

Now I'm compiling my verified findings, starting with the synchronous IPC and per-key decryption happening on every registry load, which I confirmed by tracing calls through the preload script, storage service, and multiple UI components that call getModelDisplayName repeatedly per card render.

I want to flag that my earlier benchmark used a fake localStorage bridge that didn't capture this slowdown, so the real desktop app suffers more here than my initial perf numbers suggested—worth noting since it affects that earlier conclusion.

Next is the full job list rewrite happening synchronously on every job change, which persists through the sync IPC path on desktop—I verified this directly in the job persistence code and the store implementation.

Then there's a hydration mismatch (React error #418) triggered every time jobs exist on load: the static HTML shows an empty state for the hidden image-generation panel, but the client immediately reads storage on mount and discovers actual jobs, forcing React to discard the server-rendered HTML and re-render from scratch. The fix is to defer reading storage until after mount, or only render job-dependent UI once mounted.

I'm also noting the startup bundle is bloated at 1787 KB with no lazy loading across the seven workspaces, and heavy libraries sit directly in the startup chunk — dynamic imports for canvas/gif/prompt-gallery components and lazy-loading heavy compression libraries at their point of use would help.

History virtualization is another issue: a day group with many jobs renders every card at once instead of virtualizing rows, something I confirmed by checking the list component directly.

Now I'm looking at how the desktop app converts stored images on load.

Model list and download endpoints use a 30-minute default timeout, so per-route timeouts need fixing. The text proxy also doesn't cancel upstream requests when the client disconnects, which keeps billing tokens running — a medium concern, along with shutdown behavior deleting interrupted task files on restart and the startup sequence running quick_check on every launch.

On the settings side, text model API keys always get sent to aioss.cc regardless of baseUrl, which I confirmed across model-endpoints.ts, nova-models.ts, and server.js — this is a real privacy disclosure issue since the settings UI no longer even shows a Base URL input for text models. Also, selecting a preset overwrites the name/modelId/baseUrl/limits but keeps the existing key, meaning switching presets on a relay config could send that relay's key to aioss.cc instead.

I'm also verifying that empty baseUrl values fall back to the fixed URL, that saving requires both an image model and text model configured (blocking image-only users), and that the "检查模型" check reads from the saved registry rather than draft edits — so unsaved changes get tested against old values, and the check can produce false negatives for models not listed via /v1/models even when they actually work. I've also noted that closing the settings dialog silently discards edits without confirmation, and there are gaps in Base URL validation still to look at.

Continuing through the remaining issues: defaults silently change on every keystroke, a corrupted registry JSON file (unguarded JSON.parse) would break everything, and several relay features are missing (per-model stream toggle, custom headers, timeout, test-generate). On the security side, the web backend binds to 0.0.0.0 with no auth unless a desktop token is present, and the model-list proxy fetches an arbitrary client-supplied baseUrl, creating an SSRF risk — though the desktop mode itself stays safe since it's bound to localhost with a token. This matters mainly for Docker/web deployments since the project ships a Dockerfile.

Binding to 0.0.0.0 is actually necessary inside Docker for port mapping, so the real fix isn't switching the default host but adding proper access control and SSRF guards on the proxy endpoints — I want to phrase that nuance carefully rather than just saying "default to localhost." **性能（桌面端最明显）**

1. **读模型配置会卡界面。**
   - 原因：桌面端的 `config.get` 是同步 IPC（[preload.js:15](desktop/preload.js:15)）。每读一次模型注册表，主进程都要把所有模型的密钥逐个解密（[storage-service.js:77](desktop/storage/storage-service.js:77)），而且没有缓存。能力判断每次都会重读（[model-capabilities.ts:31](frontend/src/lib/model-capabilities.ts:31)）；每张历史卡片要调两次 `getModelDisplayName`（[HistoryJobList.tsx:197](frontend/src/components/workspace/results/HistoryJobList.tsx:197)）；在历史里搜索时，每输入一个字，每条记录还要再调一次。
   - 之前改界面时做的帧率测试用的是模拟的桌面接口，没经过 IPC 和解密，所以没测到这一项。真实桌面端在这里会更慢。
   - 建议：在内存里缓存一份注册表，保存或收到 `nova-model-registry-updated` 时刷新；密钥只在真正发请求时再读取。
2. **任务每变一次，整张任务表都要同步重写一遍。**
   - 原因：`persistJobs` 在 `setJobs` 里调用 `saveJobs`（[useWorkspaceJobs.ts:79](frontend/src/hooks/useWorkspaceJobs.ts:79)），把全部任务序列化后通过同步 IPC 写入 SQLite。任务状态轮询每更新一次也会触发。任务越多越慢。
   - 建议：改成按条异步写入（桌面端已经有 `generation-jobs` 记录空间），或者防抖约 500ms 再写。
3. **每次启动都会有一次水合失败（实测）。**
   - 原因：静态 HTML 里预渲染的生图面板显示"共 0 条"，而客户端第一帧就从存储里读出了历史（`useState(loadInitialJobs)`，[useWorkspaceJobs.ts:31](frontend/src/hooks/useWorkspaceJobs.ts:31)）。两边文字对不上，React 抛出 #418，丢掉预渲染结果，改在客户端重新渲染。
   - 建议：挂载完成后再读存储，或者只在挂载后渲染依赖历史数据的部分。
4. **启动时加载的 JS 偏大（实测）。**
   - 现状：首页启动要加载 9 个脚本，共约 1.79MB（未压缩），其中 page 包就有 721KB。7 个工作区全是静态导入，整个项目没有一处 `next/dynamic`；gifenc、fflate、localforage 和 jszip 也打进了启动就会加载的 902 包（399KB）。
   - 建议：画布、动图、素材、反推和提示词广场改为按需加载；打包和编码库等到用的时候再 `import()`。
5. **历史列表的虚拟化粒度太粗。** 现在按"天"分组做虚拟化，同一天的卡片会一次全部渲染（[HistoryJobList.tsx:461](frontend/src/components/workspace/results/HistoryJobList.tsx:461)）。一天生成几百张，就会一次挂上几百张卡片。建议改成按行虚拟化。
6. **桌面端启动时，会把所有历史参考图都转成 data URL**（[job-store.ts:172](frontend/src/lib/job-store.ts:172)）：逐个读文件再做 base64 编码，历史越多，启动越慢、内存占用越高。建议等用到时再读。
7. **后端并发和内存。**
   - 现状：默认最多 50 个任务同时跑（[server.js:23](backend/server.js:23)）。流式请求默认开启，但后端会把整个响应读进内存才解析，中间的预览帧直接丢掉（[server.js:1143](backend/server.js:1143)）。一张 4K 图的 base64 约 10–20MB，并发一高，内存峰值就很大。
   - 建议：桌面端把并发降到 4–8；流式默认关闭（界面本来也不显示预览帧），或者改成边收边解析。

**后端稳定性**

8. **超时只管到响应头为止。** 响应头一到，计时器就被清掉，之后只剩 30 分钟的全局空闲超时；模型列表和图片下载也沿用这 30 分钟（[server.js:1318](backend/server.js:1318)）。建议按接口分别设上限，比如模型列表 20 秒、下载 2 分钟。
9. **文本代理不会取消上游请求。** 关掉对话后，上游的流还在继续跑、继续计费（[server.js:2140](backend/server.js:2140)）。
10. **流式失败后的回退太窄。** 只有报错文字命中特定正则时才回退到非流式（[server.js:1471](backend/server.js:1471)）。另外，报错里只要带 timeout 或 abort，就一律显示成"请求超时"或"网络连接失败"，原始状态码丢失。
11. **退出时的处理。** 有任务在跑时退出，会等 8 秒后强制结束后端（[backend-process.js:111](desktop/backend-process.js:111)）；下次启动时，中断任务里已经生成好的图片也会被一起删掉。

**设置**

12. **文本模型的密钥一律发往 aioss.cc**（[model-endpoints.ts:35](frontend/src/lib/model-endpoints.ts:35)、[server.js:2087](backend/server.js:2087)）。修正我上次的说法：文本模型表单里现在根本没有 Base URL 输入框，不是"填了不生效"。但协议里有 Claude、Gemini 等选项，用户填官方密钥，也会被发到 aioss.cc。建议：要么真正支持每个模型自定义地址，要么在密钥输入框旁边写清楚这一点。
13. **切换内置模板会覆盖掉原来的配置。** 名称、模型 ID、地址和各项上限都会被重置，但密钥保留（[SettingsModal.tsx:267](frontend/src/components/SettingsModal.tsx:267)）。地址留空保存时，会自动变成 aioss.cc（[nova-models.ts:276](frontend/src/lib/nova-models.ts:276)）。结果是中转站的密钥可能被发到 aioss.cc。建议：模板只填空着的字段，或者覆盖前先确认；地址为空时直接报错。
14. **只用生图也必须配一个文本模型才能保存**（[SettingsModal.tsx:334](frontend/src/components/SettingsModal.tsx:334)）。
15. **「检查模型」读的是已保存的配置，不是正在编辑的内容**（[ccode-task-client.ts:206](frontend/src/lib/ccode-task-client.ts:206)）。没保存的模型不会被检查，改过的密钥测的还是旧的。它也只看模型名在不在 `/v1/models` 列表里，所以像 `gpt-image-2.5-sunburst` 这种实际能用、但不在列表里的模型会被误报。建议：检查正在编辑的内容，加上超时，再加一个"试生成"按钮。
16. **其他问题：**
    - 关掉设置窗口时，未保存的修改会被直接丢弃；删除模型也没有确认。
    - 注册表数据损坏时，`loadRegistry` 会直接抛错，所有调用它的地方一起出错（[nova-models.ts:375](frontend/src/lib/nova-models.ts:375)）。
    - 保存失败时没有捕获错误，也没有提示。
17. **缺少中转站常用的选项**：按模型开关流式、自定义请求头、单独设置超时。

**安全（只影响网页 / Docker 部署）**

18. **后端没有鉴权。**
    - 现状：只有桌面端设置了会话令牌时才校验（[server.js:243](backend/server.js:243)）。网页或 Docker 部署时，任何能访问端口的人都能用它发任务。模型列表代理会请求客户端给出的任意地址，并把结果原样返回（[server.js:2178](backend/server.js:2178)），可能被当成跳板去访问内网。
    - 建议：Docker 里必须监听 0.0.0.0，所以关键在加访问控制，并禁止代理访问内网和本机地址。桌面端只监听 127.0.0.1 并带令牌，不受影响。
19. **网页版的密钥和备份。** 网页版的密钥明文存在 localStorage，备份时会原样打进 zip（[backup-utils.ts:30](frontend/src/lib/backup-utils.ts:30)）；导入备份会先清空现有数据，不做确认。桌面端的密钥由系统加密存储，备份时也会去掉。

- 第一批：改动小、收益大，第 1、2、3、7、13、14、15 条。
- 第二批：按需加载、按行虚拟化，加上后端的超时、取消、回退和退出，即第 4、5、8–11 条。
- 第三批：准备部署网页版时再做，第 18、19 条。

I also need to make sure the cache gets invalidated when other paths write the registry key directly (like backup restore flows), and think about whether returning a cheap structured clone of a small registry object is the safest way to avoid mutation bugs entirely.

For jszip, AgentImageGallery still imports it statically since it's part of the default startup tab, so I'll convert its zip download call to a dynamic import instead. Gifenc in gif-encoder.ts is lower priority but could similarly be converted to a dynamic import inside the encode function if that function is async — I'll check that later.

I'm deciding whether to edit the imports or the effect block first in useAgentChat.ts since they're too far apart to combine into one edit, and I'll go with fixing the effect block now, swapping the `hasAnyApiKey` check to use `hasTextModelConfigured` and switching from `useEffect` to `useLayoutEffect` for the API key refresh listener.

Trying to avoid a second edit, I consider defining the helper elsewhere—but a component can't be declared inline within JSX, and even placing it in a separate file still requires adding an import to WorkspaceShell's existing import block. So I'll just accept that WorkspaceShell needs two edits total.

For the import turn, I'll add the new component's import near the other dynamic imports at the top, and simultaneously create the new file for it. I also double-check that calling setVisited during render in the child is safe in React 19 since it just triggers an immediate re-render before commit.

Next I'm locating the handleUpdateImageModel function to edit its builtin preset branch, which sets protocol, name, and modelId from the preset while preserving customized fields elsewhere.

Writing the untouched-field logic...

But I'm noticing an edge case: selecting a preset on a model whose modelId was customized under the same protocol would preserve that custom modelId rather than overwrite it, which conflicts with the original feature request that presets should fill in the model id directly.

But if the user then picks a different preset like Sunburst, that custom modelId no longer matches the previous value, so it stays as the manually typed string instead of updating—which feels wrong since the user explicitly chose Sunburst.

So the real fix: baseUrl is the sensitive field (leak risk) and should be preserved if customized, along with the name for readability, but modelId/protocol/limits should always apply from the template since that's the whole point of switching presets.

I'm checking that the default draft's name and baseUrl start empty so the "untouched" check correctly fills them in for new models while leaving user edits intact.

Now moving to ccode-task-client.ts, I'm adding a 20-second timeout to the fetch call for the proxy URL, and updating the not-found message to clarify that some relay stations don't list all their models, so a missing entry doesn't necessarily mean it can't generate images.

Extending edit range...

I'm also noting other spots to revisit later: the proxy/models 30-minute timeout, the AgentImageGallery lazy jszip import, and the AssetsWorkspace hydration effect that saves sort/viewSize settings on mount—flagging these for a later batch rather than handling now.

Working through the ordering issue: if I restore settings via useLayoutEffect, React's passive effects from the first render still fire with default values first, briefly overwriting storage before the restored values get saved again on the next pass—so the transient overwrite resolves itself and the final stored value ends up correct.

More importantly, since AssetsWorkspace is now lazily mounted with ssr:false, it's never server-rendered, so the whole hydration mismatch problem disappears for it entirely. The same logic applies to CanvasWorkspace and PromptGallery once they're set to ssr:false—their hydration issues go away too, leaving only GifGenerationWorkspace and ReversePromptForm still needing attention since they remain server-rendered.

I'm laying out the concrete edits for this turn: converting the effect block in useAgentChat.ts to useLayoutEffect with proper model-configuration checks, wiring up a new MountOnFirstVisit component and importing it into WorkspaceShell, updating handleUpdateImageModel in SettingsModal, and adjusting the fetch timeout and hints in ccode-task-client.ts. The following turn will handle the imports and the larger tab-region edit in WorkspaceShell before moving to build and test.

Still writing response parsing logic...

I'm weighing whether to split the edits into smaller, safer pieces to avoid mismatches—maybe editing the fetch line separately from the message and catch block, or just doing it all as one combined edit.

I'll do the full block as one edit, adding a timeout signal to the fetch call and updating the error handling to distinguish timeouts from other errors, with a localized message. I still need to define the timeout constant, so I'll add it inside the function to keep it a single edit.

For the SettingsModal update, I'm checking the existing code that applies a built-in image preset's fields onto the model, and confirming that the `model` variable from the map callback is already in scope for the edit.

I'm also planning to add an import for the new `MountOnFirstVisit` component into WorkspaceShell, verifying the import line is unique in the file. Then I'm writing the `MountOnFirstVisit` component itself, which uses state to track whether a tab has ever been activated and keeps its children mounted once they've first appeared, so tabs don't reload their heavy content every time the user switches back to them.

Batch-one settings changes are done: saving works with image models only, an empty Base URL blocks the save, and "检查模型" checks the draft being edited. The heavy workspaces in `WorkspaceShell` are now dynamic imports. Next I'm doing the remaining pieces:

- **Agent panel:** restores key status and the two toggles before the first paint, and now only checks for a text model.
- **Template switching:** keeps a Base URL and display name you've already customized; the model ID still follows the template.
- **"检查模型":** 20-second timeout, and a clearer message when a model "isn't in the list".
- **New `MountOnFirstVisit` component:** Canvas, Assets and Prompt Gallery mount on first visit and stay mounted after that, so switching tabs doesn't lose their state.

I'm weighing options for making the timeout cover the full response body read, not just headers: proxy/model calls need a shorter timeout while image downloads need a much longer one, and text proxy currently just uses the default. Since the body is read immediately by response.text() in the image parsing paths, the simplest fix seems to be adding a mode to fetchWithTimeout that keeps the timer alive until the body is consumed, rather than restructuring every call site.

That approach feels hacky, so let me reconsider the auditor's finding about timeouts not limiting total request time — once headers arrive, only undici's 30-minute idle timer between chunks applies, and for image generation that's a reasonable enough ceiling since indefinite body trickling is mostly a theoretical edge case rather than the real problem.

The more concrete issue is that model listing and download routes wait the full 30 minutes when they shouldn't, so per-route timeouts would fix that. I'm weighing whether to build a fetchWithTimeout wrapper that also handles body completion, versus just passing AbortSignal.timeout directly into fetch to keep things simple.

Passing AbortSignal.timeout directly seems cleanest since it stays active through both headers and body reads and cleans itself up when fired, with no meaningful leak risk. But I need to handle the case where the caller also supplies its own signal (like a client-close abort), which means combining signals with AbortSignal.any.

I'm defining a wrapper that combines a timeout-based abort signal with any caller-provided signal, ensuring the deadline spans the whole request including body streaming, not just until headers arrive.
